Maeda was set to face the reigning World Featherweight Champion Jack "Nonpareil" Dempsey in a non-title fight in 1913 , but Maeda suffered an injury and was unable to fight.

 Maeda defeated Rafael Garcia in Mexico City in 1917 . In May 1918 , Maeda won the Mexican National Lightweight Championship.
 Maeda fought in the United States again in August 1919 . He lost to Jack Britton at the Polo Grounds in New York .
In July 1920 , Maeda made his return to Japan. He toured the country and defeated a series of challengers. He lost to Yoshio Shirai and was defeated in a rematch with Britton.
 Maeda won the Japanese National Lightweight Championship in May 1922 . He defeated Tatsuo Hayakawa twice and defended the belt successfully in a series of bouts.

The 1978 Pacific hurricane season officially started on May 15, 1978, and lasted until November 30, 1978. These dates conventionally delimit the period of each year when most tropical cyclones form in the northeastern Pacific Ocean .
The season's activity was slightly above normal, producing a total of 14 named storms, 6 hurricanes, and 3 major hurricanes. The season's activity was attributed to the presence of El Niño -Southern Oscillation.
Tropical Storm Juliette was the first storm of the season. It formed from a trough of low pressure south of Mexico . Juliette moved west-northwestward, and gradually became better organized, attaining tropical storm status on July 23. The storm then turned to the north and quickly intensified into a hurricane on July 25. Juliette reached its peak intensity of 115 mph (185 km/h) on the same day. The storm maintained this peak intensity for almost 24 hours before slowly weakening. On July 26, Juliette made landfall on the coast of the Baja California Peninsula , and was subsequently downgraded to a tropical storm. Hurricane Juliette then quickly dissipated over the western United States.
Hurricane Kate developed on August 12 from a tropical wave that moved across the Caribbean into the central Gulf of Mexico . Kate gradually became better organized, and attained hurricane status on August 16. The storm then turned to the north and reached its peak intensity of 115 mph (185 km/h) on August 17. Kate maintained this peak intensity for several hours as it approached the Florida Panhandle. The storm then made landfall on August 18 near Panama City, Florida and quickly weakened over land. Hurricane Kate then dissipated over Georgia on August 19.
Hurricane Linda developed from a tropical wave that moved across the Caribbean Sea into the central Gulf of Mexico . Linda gradually became better organized, and attained hurricane status on August 26. The storm then turned to the north and rapidly intensified, reaching its peak intensity of 140 mph (230 km/h) on the same day. Linda maintained this peak intensity for several hours as it approached the southern Baja California Peninsula. The storm then made landfall on the Baja California Peninsula on August 27. Hurricane Linda then moved inland over Mexico and dissipated on August 28.
The 1978 Pacific typhoon season officially started on May 15, 1978, and lasted until November 30, 1978. These dates conventionally delimit the period of each year when most tropical cyclones form in the northwestern Pacific Ocean .
The season's activity was slightly below normal, producing a total of 23 tropical storms, 9 typhoons, and 4 major typhoons.
Typhoon Barbara is the first storm of the season. Barbara was an extremely large typhoon with a diameter of 680 nm. Barbara developed from a tropical depression, which was caused by the interaction between a tropical wave and a trough of low pressure. Typhoon Barbara intensified into a super typhoon with 165 mph (265 km/h) winds. Barbara then tracked across the northern Philippines and China . Typhoon Barbara struck the Philippines as a Category 4 typhoon before making landfall on China as a Category 3 typhoon. The storm caused 139 deaths and $690 million dollars in damage.
Super Typhoon Dotty is the second storm of the season. Dotty developed from a tropical depression, which was caused by the interaction between a tropical wave and a trough of low pressure. Typhoon Dotty intensified into a super typhoon with 185 mph (300 km/h) winds. Dotty then tracked across the northern Philippines and China . Dotty struck the Philippines as a Category 5 typhoon before making landfall on China

As the sentinel approached the room , a voice called out to him .
"I'm going to tell you the truth about the Order of the Skull and Bones," the voice said .

A native of Texas , Applewhite attended several universities and , as a young man , served in the United States Army . After fi

nally earning a bachelor's degree in sociology from the University of Texas at Austin in 1964 , Applewhite became a high school teacher in Austin and later served as a counselor at the University of Texas . He later earned a master's degree in counseling from the University of Colorado at Boulder . In 1974 , he married Diana Teets.
 Applewhite co-founded Heaven's Gate on November 22 , 1975 , with another man , Mark Walsh . Walsh soon left the group and Applewhite became its sole leader . Applewhite and the other members of Heaven's Gate believed that life on Earth was a test and that humans were being evaluated by an extraterrestrial being known as "The Watcher" .
 Applewhite and the group believed that the members of Heaven's Gate had completed their tests and would be transferred to another plane of existence known as "the Level Above Human." The group was convinced that they had been chosen for this transfer to another life by The Watcher .
The members of Heaven's Gate believed that the Level Above Human was located in the Alpha Draconis star system . It was here that they would be met by a spaceship piloted by The Watcher . Applewhite believed that this transfer would occur during a cometary near miss of the Earth on March 26 , 1997 .
Applewhite instructed all of the members of Heaven's Gate to wear all white clothing and to prepare for the move to a better life on the Level Above Human . In early 1997 , Applewhite and the members of Heaven's Gate left their homes and began living in a 12-bedroom home in Rancho Santa Fe , California . They believed that this was the last place where they would ever live .
 Applewhite instructed the members of Heaven's Gate to cut off all contact with their families and friends . They were also prohibited from using a television or radio , and were not permitted to read a newspaper or magazine . In addition , they were instructed to write letters to their families describing how they were living at the "end of the world" .
On March 26 , 1997 , Applewhite and the members of Heaven's Gate committed suicide by overdosing on vodka laced with phenobarbital . They believed that they were being transferred to the Level Above Human . 84 members of Heaven's Gate were found dead in various locations throughout Rancho Santa Fe .

New York State Route 164 ( NY 164 ) is a short state highway located entirely in the town of Patterson in northeastern Putnam C

on the border with the town of Carmel, in New York , US. One of the shortest state routes in the state, it is a north–south connector between NY 52 at the hamlet of Carmel and the western end of the Taconic State Parkway ( I-87 / NY 301 ) in the same hamlet. A connecting route, NY 164 Connector, runs from NY 52 to the parkway. The route is also known as Temple Hill Road.
The Putnam County Department of Public Works maintains the roadway from NY 52 to the parkway, including the NY 164 Connector. The New York State Department of Transportation ( NYSDOT ) is responsible for maintaining the remainder of the route within the state right-of-way.

In the 1940s, the New York State Department of Public Works ( NYSDPW ) constructed the current alignment of NY 164, which connects NY 52 in Carmel with NY 301 at the north end of the Taconic State Parkway . ## History

The 900 m ( 3 @,@ 000 ft ) East Moors Viaduct opened in 1864 with the 160 m ( 5,200 ft ) west viaduct. The viaduct was designed by the railway's chief engineer,  Sir Joseph Locke .

The 900 m ( 3 @,@ 000 ft ) East Moors Viaduct is built in three sections, each composed of 26 arches, for a total of 81 arches. The 160 m ( 5,200 ft ) west viaduct is 26 arches. The Chrono series is a video game franchise developed and published by Square Enix ( formerly Square ) . It began in 1995 with

1995 's Chrono Trigger , which was directed by Akira Toriyama and was one of the most acclaimed role-playing games of its time. The series has since continued to receive critical acclaim, and has been named "one of the greatest series ever" by 1UP .com .
The series takes place in a multiverse that contains several parallel worlds, where the main characters can travel to different times and places, thereby affecting the course of history. The first three games in the series were released on the Super Nintendo Entertainment System , PlayStation , and PC, while Chrono Cross was released on the PlayStation and Nintendo 64 . The games typically feature a large cast of characters with a large amount of storyline and dialogue, and are generally considered to be among the best role-playing games of their respective time.
Chrono Cross was the last game in the series to be released, until 2011 , when Chrono Trigger was released on the Nintendo DS , and later on the PlayStation Portable and PlayStation 3 .
The series is centered around the main character, a nameless boy from the fictional town of Termina, who is unwittingly involved in a time traveling adventure that spans multiple eras and fictional worlds, just as his two best friends, the twin brothers Frog and Robo. The main characters of each game are different, but they share similar personalities, such as the desire to stop the end of the world, and are often accompanied by a mysterious girl who is usually the one to introduce them to the adventures that await them.
Many of the games in the series feature elements from other genres, including action role-playing games ( Chrono Trigger ), real-time strategy ( Chrono Cross ), and puzzle games ( Chrono Cross ). However, the games are generally considered to be role-playing games, with the Chrono Trigger and Chrono Cross games being considered to be among the best in the genre.
The Chrono series has been called "one of the greatest series ever" by 1UP .com , and has been praised for its story and characters, as well as its gameplay.

I. hollingtoniensis ( also spelled I. hollingtonensis ) , described by Lydekker in 1889 has variously been considered a synonym

of I. priscilla (Lydekker, 1885) or I. p. rupestris (Lydekker, 1885), and a separate species. 

## Description

The single specimen, described by Lydekker, measured 5.5 inches (14 cm) in length. It was a robust lizard, with broad, shield-like scales on the flanks and large, round scales on the dorsal surface of the head. The body was black, with yellow lines on the sides of the neck and back.

## Distribution and habitat

The only known specimen of the species was collected near Hollington Lodge, in the south of the county of Kent, England. It was found in a ruined building, and at one time was thought to have been a domestic pet.

The Canadian attack on San Leonardo by the Seaforth Highlanders of Canada began late on 5 December 1943 with A Company establis

The Canadian attack on San Leonardo by the Seaforth Highlanders of Canada began late on 5 December 1943 with A Company establishing a blocking position at the mouth of the Fosso del Lupo (Wolf Ravine) and other defiles to the west of the village. A few hours later, B Company moved up to the village itself. The Seaforths faced a German force of about 100 men. Both the Seaforths and the Germans were surprised by the attack. The Seaforths took the village and by the next morning, the Canadian force had expanded to include the Black Watch of Canada, and a company of the Royal Hamilton Light Infantry. The Germans took up positions on the high ground to the north of the village, and a bitter fighting continued for the next 10 days. A Canadian attack on 15 December was repulsed with severe losses. As the battle raged, the Germans were reinforced by a battalion of the 90th Light Division, and the Canadian force was reinforced by a company of the South Saskatchewan Regiment. The Canadians were finally reinforced by a company of the Leicestershire Regiment and a company of the Royal Army Service Corps. The 32nd Armoured Regiment (The Sherbrooke Fusiliers) provided support, and the 1st Parachute Squadron of the Royal Canadian Horse Artillery (the Fort Garry Horse) brought in 85-mm howitzer support. The Seaforths were relieved by the 1st Battalion, the Royal Hamilton Light Infantry, on 20 December, and the battalion was relieved by the 1st Battalion, the Royal Regiment of Canada, on 22 December. The Germans were relieved by the 3rd Battalion, the 16th Panzer Grenadier Regiment on 23 December. The Germans continued to fight in the area until 27 December, when they attempted a breakout. The Canadian force was reorganized and the 1st Battalion, the Royal Regiment of Canada, took up blocking positions in and around the village. The fighting continued for another week as the Royal Regiment of Canada (with support from the 1st Battalion, the Sherbrooke Fusiliers) and the 32nd Armoured Regiment (The Sherbrooke Fusiliers) worked to block the exits from the village. The Germans eventually withdrew, and the 32nd Armoured Regiment (The Sherbrooke Fusiliers) took up blocking positions on the high ground to the north of the village. The Seaforth Highlanders of Canada was relieved by the 1st Battalion, the Royal Regiment of Canada on 25 December 1943. The German force was relieved by the 295th Infantry Division during the night of 28–29 December.

DE 261 begins at an interchange with US 202 and the northern terminus of DE 141 north of Alapocas Run State Park near Fairfax ,

Delaware . It heads southwest through the northern suburbs of Wilmington, and intersects the northern terminus of DE 72 before crossing the Brandywine Creek into the city of Wilmington . In downtown Wilmington , DE 261 runs parallel to the North-South Freeway (I-95/US 13), intersecting the southern terminus of DE 1 (the Delaware Memorial Bridge). DE 261 runs south through the Wilmington Riverfront and the Shipyards neighborhood, ending at an interchange with I-95/US 13 south of the Port of Wilmington . The entire length of DE 261 is a four-lane road.

DE 261 was first designated in 1939, running from US 13 and DE 141 in Fairfax northward to Wilmington. In 1945, DE 261 was extended southward to I-95/US 13 in Wilmington. DE 261 was extended to DE 1 (the Delaware Memorial Bridge) in 1947, replacing DE 261A. In 1966, DE 261 was extended south to its current southern terminus.

A tropical wave developed into a tropical depression early on September 10 , while located about midway between Cape Verde and

the Lesser Antilles. It gradually intensified and became Tropical Storm Irwin on the 12th, while located about 650 miles (1,050 km) east of the Leeward Islands. Upon reaching hurricane status, Irwin reached its peak intensity on September 14, with winds of 130 mph (215 km/h) and a minimum central pressure of 954 mbar (28.18 inHg). Irwin gradually weakened, and after moving over the Mona Passage, it weakened into a tropical storm and then a tropical wave on the 21st. It dissipated a day later near the Yucatán Peninsula.

Tropical Storm Irwin (1971)

In the Lesser Antilles, Irwin produced heavy rainfall and gusty winds, which caused minor damage. However, in the Yucatán Peninsula, the storm caused the death of one person. In Florida, Irwin produced heavy rainfall, which caused localized flooding.

On September 9, a tropical wave emerged off the coast of Africa. It moved west-northwestward, and emerged into the Atlantic Ocean on the 10th. The next day, a tropical depression formed while located about midway between Cape Verde and the Lesser Antilles. The depression gradually intensified, and on September 12, it became Tropical Storm Irwin while located about 650 miles (1,050 km) east of the Leeward Islands. Upon reaching hurricane status on September 12, Irwin reached its peak intensity later that day, with winds of 130 mph (215 km/h) and a minimum central pressure of 954 mbar (28.18 inHg). Irwin gradually weakened, and after moving over the Mona Passage, it weakened into a tropical storm on September 14. It then continued to weaken, and degenerated into a tropical wave on the 21st. Irwin dissipated near the Yucatán Peninsula on September 22.

## Preparations and impact

In the Lesser Antilles, Irwin produced heavy rainfall and gusty winds, which caused minor damage. However, in the Yucatán Peninsula, the storm caused the death of one person. In Florida, Irwin produced heavy rainfall, which caused localized flooding.

Jarvis scored the only goal in York 's first win since October 2013 , a 1 – 0 home victory over Morecambe on New Year 's Day .

On 28 January 2014, Jarvis scored the only goal of the game in a 1 – 0 away victory over Torquay United , his first goal in 58 appearances for the club. Jarvis scored another goal in York 's next fixture, a 2 – 0 home win over Bury on 1 February 2014.
On 25 March 2014, Jarvis scored a hat-trick in York 's 3 – 2 win over Aldershot Town in the FA Trophy at the York Community Stadium. Jarvis scored his third goal of the game, and his 13th of the season, with a 25-yard strike in the 90th minute to secure the victory. On 29 March 2014, Jarvis was named in the League Two Team of the Week for his performance in the 3 – 2 win over Aldershot Town. On 12 April 2014, Jarvis scored again as York secured a 2 – 0 away victory over Morecambe at the Globe Arena. The victory secured York 's place in the League Two play-off Final at Wembley on 11 May 2014.
On 11 May 2014, Jarvis scored in the 2014 League Two play-off Final at Wembley, but it was not enough to prevent his side from losing 1 – 0 to Fleetwood Town , who secured promotion to League One.
On 13 June 2014, Jarvis was appointed as a player-coach at York City. On 19 May 2015, Jarvis announced his retirement from football in order to join the coaching staff at York City. York City were relegated from League Two at the end of the 2015–16 season.
On 15 November 2016, Jarvis was appointed as interim manager of York City. After a 2 – 0 away win over Northampton Town on 26 November 2016, Jarvis left his role as interim manager to return to his coaching role at the club.
Jarvis was appointed as caretaker manager of York City again on 6 January 2017, following the departure of Nigel Worthington. Following a 3 – 1 away win over Hartlepool United on 14 January 2017, Jarvis was appointed as the permanent manager of York City.
On 6 June 2018, it was announced that Jarvis had left his role as manager of York City following the club's relegation from League Two at the end of the 2017–18 season.
On 31 August 2018, Jarvis returned to York City as a coach.
On 28 September 2018, Jarvis was appointed as caretaker manager of York City for the second time, following the departure of Gary Mills. On 2 January 2019, Jarvis was appointed as permanent manager of York City for the second time, following the departure of Martin Gray.
Having played at youth level for England up to under-17 level, Jarvis was called up by the England under-18s squad for the game against France on 5 September 2001.

ours de Piano , set up to promote young musicians . Perhaps the lesson of the 1859 -1861 Concours de Piano of the Paris Conservatoire was still too fresh in his memory , with Liszt and Saint-Saëns winning the first two prizes and Alkan - the only teacher , at the Conservatoire - the third .
a) The first , on 13 April 1873 , was for the best piece in the style of Chopin . b) The second , on 20 April 1873 , was for the best piece in the style of Bach . The programme included fugues by Bach (BWV 589 and 582) , following by a Schubert Sonata in A minor (D 784) , and concluded with the Prelude in A major (Op. 31 No. 2) by Alkan .
Alcan did not give a name to the fugue by Bach . This is the same fugue as the fifth subject of the fugue in C major (Op. 39 No. 5) .

 e) The fifth , on 11 May 1873 , was for the best piece in the style of Beethoven . The programme included a sonata by Beethoven (Op. 57 No. 3 in C minor) , followed by a Schubert Sonata in A minor (D 784) , and concluded with the Prelude in C major (Op. 31 No. 5) by Alkan .

Commander Katherine Pulaski is a fictional medical doctor in the American science fiction television series Star Trek : The Nex

Star Trek: The Next Generation. comic book series. She is a Starfleet officer who was assigned to the science vessel USS Enterprise-D.
The character was played by actress Beverly Crusher in the series' first season.

As a result, Gibberman was replaced with Crusher.
Pulaski made her first appearance in the episode "Encounter at Farpoint" and made her final appearance in the episode "The Neutral Zone".
In the show's second season, Pulaski was written out of the series.
She remained a member of the Starfleet Medical Corps, and appeared in the novels and comic books set in the Star Trek universe.
In January 2005, a petition was launched to have Pulaski inducted into the Star Trek Hall of Fame.

Baker was born in Long Beach , California and raised in what he considered a " stifling , Republican Southern Californian house

hold." The child of a military father , Baker has described his childhood as "a very, very strict upbringing." He attended high school in the Chicago suburb of Deerfield , Illinois , where he set his sights on becoming a concert pianist. Baker stated that he had wanted to go to New York City to study at Juilliard , but his father insisted that he attend a state school .  After being accepted to the University of Texas , Austin , where he studied music , he later transferred to the University of Southern California , where he studied theater .
In 1997, Baker began his career in Los Angeles in a small theater company called the Road Theatre. He had one of the lead roles in the play, "The 1940s Radio Hour". In 2001, Baker began to make appearances in small independent films such as "Blood Out" and "The Cooler", both of which starred William H. Macy . Baker also starred in some episodes of the television series "Andy Richter Controls the Universe".
In 2004, Baker starred in the lead role in the independent film "Hard Candy", which was directed by David Slade . The film premiered at the 2005 Sundance Film Festival . According to Box Office Mojo, the film grossed $8,765,967 worldwide. In 2006, Baker starred in the independent film "The Lookout", which was directed by Scott Frank and co-starred Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Matthew Goode and Isla Fisher .
In 2007, Baker starred with Liam Neeson and Pierce Brosnan in the film "Breakfast on Pluto", and co-starred with Mickey Rourke and Kim Basinger in "Lady in the Water", directed by M. Night Shyamalan . In 2008, Baker starred with Hilary Swank in the psychological thriller "The Reaping", which was directed by Stephen Hopkins and also starred David Morrissey .

The film is based on the play of the same name, which was written by Richard Bean and directed by Jonathan Demme . The film also stars Bill Nighy , Kelly Reilly , and James D'Arcy . The film was released in 2010.
In 2009, Baker starred in the Canadian independent film "The Stone Angel", which was directed by Kari Skogland and co-starred Ellen Burstyn .
Baker has been cast as the lead role in the film "The Mechanic", which is a remake of the 1972 film of the same name. The film is scheduled to be released on January 28, 2011.

Today , some prerogative powers are directly exercised by ministers without the approval of Parliament , including the powers o

grant state pensions , to impose information requirements on citizens , to conduct diplomatic relations with foreign states , and to detain immigrants for up to 24 hours . In many of these areas , parliamentary approval is sought only occasionally or for a particular purpose .
Separately , the House of Lords has retained the power to reject or amend Bills passed by the House of Commons . As a result , the government has been forced to accept the amendment of a number of its Bills in the Lords , including those on hunting , the Human Rights Act , and the Serious Organised Crime and Police Act . The government has also recently proposed constitutional reforms to reduce the influence of the House of Lords .
The powers of the devolved parliaments and assemblies are set out in each of their respective Acts . The Scottish Parliament retains the power to make legislation in all areas which do not fall within the legislative competence of the UK Parliament , and the Welsh Assembly has the power to make legislation in all areas that are within the competence of the UK Parliament . In Northern Ireland , the Northern Ireland Assembly has the power to legislate on most matters , but the UK Parliament has the power to legislate in a number of areas.
The Sewel Convention , which requires the UK Parliament to refrain from legislating on devolved matters without the consent of the devolved legislatures , has been interpreted as preventing the UK Parliament from legislating to require the devolved legislatures to amend existing legislation without their consent . This means that the UK Parliament cannot use the Parliament Acts to require the Scottish Parliament and the Welsh Assembly to amend legislation passed in those Parliaments .
The UK Parliament , however , retains significant powers over the devolved institutions , including the power to legislate with respect to the funding of the devolved institutions and to amend the competences of the devolved institutions .
 The UK Parliament is the legislature of the United Kingdom and is bicameral , consisting of the House of Lords and the House of Commons . The House of Commons is the lower house , and is elected by the people . The House of Lords is the upper house .
 The House of Commons is elected for a fixed term of five years , with general elections being held on the first Thursday in May in the fifth year after the previous election . The House of Lords is not subject to a fixed term , but members of the House must retire by age 75 (or 22 years of service) . The House of Lords is able to delay an Act of Parliament for a maximum of two years by passing a vote of dissent (or , in the case of a bill that affects the House of Lords itself , by passing a vote of disagreement ) . If the House of Commons passes the bill a third time , the bill may become law without the consent of the House of Lords .
 The House of Lords is able to delay an Act of Parliament for a maximum of two years by passing a vote of dissent (or , in the case of a bill that affects the House of Lords itself , by passing a vote of disagreement ) . If the House of Commons passes the bill a third time , the bill may become law without the consent of the House of Lords .
 The House of Lords , however , retains a number of powers over the government , including the power to delay ministerial appointments and to delay legislation by passing a vote of dissent .
 The power to delay legislation is subject to a number of limitations . Legislation that is subject to the House of Lords' power to delay cannot be subject to a vote of dissent if it would facilitate the government in carrying out its program during the election period . The House of Lords cannot delay legislation which impinges upon the sovereignty of Parliament or to which the House of Commons has already given its approval in a third reading . Furthermore , the House of Lords cannot delay legislation that has been approved in a third reading and then passed by the Scottish Parliament or the Welsh Assembly .
 The Royal Prerogative is the residue of discretionary executive power exercisable by the Crown , the Cabinet or ministers of the Crown . In practice , the Crown's powers are exercised by the Prime Minister and the Cabinet , and the powers of the Prime Minister and the Cabinet are exercised by ministers . The prerogative powers are not a grant of power by Parliament , and therefore do not need to be exercised in the same manner as ordinary statutory powers .

In 1900 , antiquarian George Clinch investigated the Biddenden Maids in detail . Examining the costumes of the figures on the B

iddenden church windows, he found that they wore similar clothes to those worn by the maids in the fifteenth-century illustrations. The details of the costumes are very important, because they reveal that the Biddenden Maids were not re-enactments of medieval characters, as some people assumed, but played the part of medieval characters in the nineteenth century. The maids' costumes are important for another reason. They were copied from medieval images, and so they can be used to identify the artist who produced the original images, and also to establish the date of the images.
The costumes of the Biddenden Maids suggest that they were probably painted by William Hole, who dressed the figures in the windows of Westminster Abbey, Winchester Cathedral and St Martin's, Canterbury. Hole's work on the Biddenden church windows is an important source of information on the 'female medieval' in the nineteenth century. He lived and worked in the Victorian era, yet he helped to create an image of medieval women that is still influential today.
In the same way, the Biddenden Maids were not modern dressers playing medieval dressers, but were products of their own time. The costumes of the Biddenden Maids are important because they were created by a professional artist, and they can be used to look at the nature of dress and society in the nineteenth century. The Biddenden Maids were thus a unique combination of the medieval and the modern in the Victorian era.

The starling is native to Europe, western Asia and northwest Africa. It is an introduced species in Australia, New Zealand, South Africa, the United States, Canada, and the Caribbean.
S. vulgaris has been introduced to Australia and New Zealand for both food and sport. It has become firmly established in Australia and New Zealand, and is regarded by many as an agricultural pest. It is also an unwelcome nesting species in urban environments, and has been responsible for numerous electrocutions. In New Zealand, the common starling has been classified as a "medium-sized pest species" by the New Zealand Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry.
For many years the common starling was considered to be a pest in the United Kingdom; it was frequently shot and trapped. The Birds of the British Isles by Howard Saunders (1907) has the following to say about the common starling: "The habits of the Starling, when first introduced to this country, were, doubtless, in many respects, unsuited to the climate, but they have since become thoroughly adaptable, and now abound in almost every part of the British Islands, and are almost as numerous in some of the larger towns as in the fields."
In 2011, the New Jersey Division of Fish and Wildlife reported that the starling population is declining in New Jersey, with a reduction of 70% in the number of broods in 2010 compared to a decade earlier.[3] The decline is attributed to a virus that was first detected in the state in 2004.[4]

The common starling was first described by zoologist Carl Linnaeus in 1758 in the tenth edition of his Systema Naturae under its current binomial name. The specific epithet vulgaris is the Latin for "common".
The common starling is a medium-sized passerine bird. Its length is about 25 cm (9.8 in), with a wingspan of 38 cm (15 in). It weighs about 66 g (2.3 oz). It has a long tail and predominantly glossy black plumage with a purple or green sheen. The bill is black, the iris is brown, the legs and feet are blackish-grey, and the eyes are dark brown. The sexes are similar, but the juvenile has less glossy feathers and a dull bill and eye.
The starling's call is a shriek, similar to that of the common raven. It has a variety of calls, including a chattering, chirruping, tseep, tweet, and whistling. Song is typically a slow, melodious whistle, often imitating other bird species.

The Nek was originally The Nek of Asia Minor, a part of the larger Peninsula of Asia Minor.
The Nek was first used as a name for the narrow track connecting Australia to mainland Asia during the early 19th century.

The Gregorian Tower ( Italian : Torre Gregoriana ) or Tower of the Winds ( Italian : Torre dei Venti ) is a round tower located

in Piazza di Pietra in Rome, Italy, and part of the obelisk raised by Pope Sixtus V.
The tower was built between 1585 and 1590 as part of the last construction works of Pope Sixtus V, who wanted to embellish Rome after the Sack of 1527.
It was designed by Domenico Fontana, who had previously designed the fountains of Piazza Navona and the Fontana del Tritone, and built under the direction of Giacomo della Porta.
The tower, with an octagonal base, rises 45 metres (148 ft) above the square, and has a total elevation of 64 metres (210 ft): a spiral staircase of 171 steps leads to the top.
The sculptor Ottaviano Mascherino executed the sculptures on the four faces of the tower.
On the top is a bronze weather vane depicting a cockerel.
On the terrace surrounding the tower, a bronze statue of Sixtus V by the sculptor Tommaso Ruffo was erected in 1593.
The tower was designed and built for the purpose of providing a source of fresh air for the Piazza del Popolo and the adjacent streets.
At the time, the square was the main entry point to the city from the north, and people coming from that direction would be subject to the smells and pollution of the Roman Tiber.
The tower has a circular perforated stone screen with a pipe passing through it and venting the air outside.
Today, the air is not clean, and the vents are mainly ornamental.
The tower is now a tourist attraction.
It is possible to climb to the top of the tower for a fee.
Except for the pagan goddess Fortuna, who was originally depicted in the inlaid marble floor of the Piazza di Pietra, none of the sculptures on the tower are known to have any religious significance.
It is not a Roman monument, as it does not have any kind of inscription on it.
The tower is not visible from the Vatican, although it is only 300 metres (980 ft) away.
In 2007, the tower was one of the first sites to receive free unlimited WiFi from the City of Rome.
The Tower of the Winds in Athens, Greece, which was built around 50 BCE, is often referred to as the "Greek" Tower of the Winds, to distinguish it from the tower in Rome.
Both towers are octagonal in plan, with four of the sides covered by reliefs of the eight winds, while the other four sides are plain.
Some of the reliefs on the Roman Tower were made in the workshop of the sculptor Ottaviano Mascherino, who also made those on the Tower of the Winds in Athens.
These reliefs are very similar and have been attributed to him.

The sculpture is currently attributed to a 1st-century BCE school and is thought to have been created in the province of Asia Minor.

A total of 42 species of Ficus (Moraceae) have been reported in Japan, and 13 of these are native to Japan. We collected herbarium material for all the native species and many introduced species from the 46 Japanese Herbaria that have a Ficus collection. The herbarium material consists of 2,093 dried specimens including 87 fruit specimens. Ten dried specimens of two species (F. japonica and F. squamosa ) are designated as type specimens. This is the first comprehensive collection of herbarium material for all species of Ficus in Japan. This collection will be useful for studies of plant conservation and biogeography in Japan.

Braathens South American & Far East Airtransport A / S was founded on 26 March 1946 by Ludvig G. Braathen through his shipping

and aviation companies. The airline was established with the aim of transporting goods between Norway and the Far East, but it was also a pioneer in introducing passenger air transport. The airline's first air route was from Oslo to London, but the first passenger flight flew from Oslo to Copenhagen. The airline's first aircraft were four Douglas DC-3s that were arriving during the spring of 1946.
In May 1946, Braathens South American & Far East Airtransport A / S was running two routes: Oslo – London – Copenhagen and Oslo – Stockholm – Gothenburg. The same year, Braathens South American & Far East Airtransport A / S acquired 100 percent of A / S Flyvebanen Norway. This company was established on 29 May 1946 by Ludvig G. Braathen and his brother John Braathen, and it had a fleet of four Lockheed 10s. Braathens South American & Far East Airtransport A / S's passenger traffic was initially run through A / S Flyvebanen Norway.
On 1 March 1947, Braathens South American & Far East Airtransport A / S was sold to Braathens South American & Far East Airtransport AS. The company's new name was Braathens SAFE.
The company's first international air route was from Oslo to New York, which was inaugurated on 26 October 1947. The airline was also the first to introduce the DC-4. The airline's first DC-4 flight was from Oslo to London, which was inaugurated on 19 July 1948.
The first intercontinental flight took off from Oslo on 1 February 1949. The flight was to Los Angeles and it took 47.5 hours. It was also the first time the airline had operated a 100 per cent full flight.
On 29 July 1950, the airline was hit by a crisis when a DC-4 crash-landed at Stavanger Airport. The airline had to pay a fine of NOK 150,000 and the aircraft had to be written off.
The airline's first Boeing 707 was taken into service in 1959. It was an important milestone for the airline, as it was the first time it had a jet aircraft. The first intercontinental passenger flight with a Boeing 707 was from Oslo to New York on 20 October 1959. The first intercontinental cargo flight was the same year when the airline started to transport cargo with a Boeing 707. The first transatlantic passenger flight with a Boeing 707 was from New York to Oslo on 4 October 1960.
The airline's first jet air route was from Oslo to Copenhagen, which was inaugurated on 28 March 1960. The same year, the airline started operating the Boeing 707-320C.
The airline's fleet consisted of seven Boeing 707-320Bs, one Boeing 707-320C and one Boeing 707-438. The airline was also the first to operate the Boeing 747 on an intercontinental route. The first intercontinental passenger flight with a Boeing 747 was from Oslo to New York on 27 March 1970.
The airline started operating the Boeing 747-200 on its intercontinental routes in February 1971. On 23 May 1971, the airline started to operate the Boeing 747-200 on its European routes. The same year, the airline was the first to introduce the Boeing 747-200B.
On 29 January 1972, the airline was the first to introduce the Boeing 747SP on its intercontinental routes. The same year, the airline was the first to introduce the Boeing 747-200B on its European routes.
On 27 February 1973, the airline was the first to introduce the Boeing 747-300 on its intercontinental routes. The same year, the airline was the first to introduce the Boeing 747-300 on its European routes.

nd Wickes ( DD < @-@ 47 ) classes were smaller and the much larger classes that followed ( Benson ( DD @-@ 48 to DD @-@ 57 ) and Porter ( DD @-@ 57 to DD @-@ 59 ) ) were more heavily armed. The NLF and MAAG had just recently agreed on a cease-fire in the RVN and the creation of a 27,000 man "Popular Force" to help patrol the countryside. The NLF was able to successfully push for the removal of Khánh as a precondition to the signing of the "New Epoch Agreement." Ectomycorrhizal , Amanita muscaria forms symbiotic relationships with many trees , including pine , spruce , fir , birch , and

beech .  It is commonly found in and around Sitka spruce but has also been known to form ectomycorrhizal associations with Douglas fir , lodgepole pine , and Engelmann spruce .  

Ectomycorrhizal fungi form associations with the roots of trees and help the trees absorb nutrients. The fungi obtain their nutrients from the organic matter present in the soil. This fungus is often thought to be the source of the psychoactive substance, psilocybin , an hallucinogenic compound present in the mushroom. 

The A. muscaria fungus can be found in northern latitudes from Alaska and Siberia to Europe and North America.

Red Lake, located in northern Minnesota, was originally part of the territory; it became part of the state when Minnesota was admitted to the union in 1858. The annuity traditionally was a one-time payment made to the Indians. In 1856, the government established an annuity pay­ment of $20,000 to be made in 48 equal installments over a 30-year period. The government also agreed to make annual payments to the band until 1894, at which time the band would receive the final payment and the land would be sold.

" Caught Up " is a song by American R & B singer Usher . It was written by Ryan Toby , Andre Harris , Vidal Davis and Jason Boy

kins for the singer's third studio album, 8701 (2001). Production was handled by Toby, Harris and Davis with the latter two providing background vocals as well. The song reflects on a relationship that has gone sour and is reaching its breaking point. It has been labelled a grungy R&B anthem and the sound of the background vocals have been compared to that of Eric Clapton.
" Caught Up " was sent to contemporary R&B radio stations in early 2002, and was later included on the soundtrack to the 2002 film Barbershop . It was a moderate success, charting in the US and the UK. It was later included on the US reissue of 8701. A remix featuring Clipse was included on the US edition of Usher's 2004 album Confessions , peaking at number 77 on the US Billboard Hot 100 and becoming his third number one on the US Billboard Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs chart.

Many proteins are involved in the process of cell signaling and signal transduction . Some proteins , such as insulin , are ext

racellular , and must be internalised before they can be effective. They are broken down into smaller peptides by proteases , which are also called proteolytic enzymes . A protease is any enzyme that breaks peptide bonds, and is also called a peptidase, a peptide hydrolase or a protease. Proteases are associated with a broad range of biological processes, some of which are beneficial and others of which are harmful.
Protease activity is regulated by inhibitors. Protease inhibitors (PIs) are a class of proteins which bind to and block proteases. All PIs are extremely small and highly specific (some are smaller than 2000 daltons) . They bind to the protease's active site, preventing it from functioning properly.
Proteases are important in a wide range of biological processes, including the development of cancer , autoimmune disorders , and infectious diseases . They are also used extensively in the food and pharmaceutical industries, as well as in research laboratories.

One of Walpole 's major novels of the early post @-@ war period was The Cathedral , which unlike much of his fiction was not da

ubed with the label 'fiction'. The novel was subtitled 'A Poem' and, as he put it, 'I have stuck to the regular Rules, and made it a perfect Epic Poem'. Whatever its merits, it was never popular and has been largely forgotten.
In the poem, the hero is a man called _Heathcliff_ , a Celtic name, who grew up in a household of the Earnshaws, on the Yorkshire moors, and who, after a series of misadventures, marries the young Catherine Earnshaw. Their life at Wuthering Heights is disturbed by the arrival of a man called _Linton_ , who is the son of the previous tenant of the household, and is weak and sickly. To avenge himself for Catherine 's refusal to marry him, _Heathcliff_ abducts Linton and then sets out to waylay his son Hareton, who is a strong and handsome young man. The tale is told by a man called Lockwood, who moves into the empty house.
In 1823, the novel was published in three volumes, and the first volume ends with the events described above. In 1847, when the poem was republished in a single volume, the story was continued with the events after the death of Catherine, and the death of _Heathcliff_ , by a new narrator, one of the younger generation of the Earnshaws.
It is not surprising that the novel was later forgotten, for it is a hopelessly confused and disjointed tale. The first volume is full of descriptions of the landscape, the weather, the landscape, the weather, and so on, and the characters are introduced in a rather haphazard fashion. The hero's name is never explained, and when it is discovered that he is a moorland Celt by birth, and not a Yorkshireman, the reader is completely mystified. The entire second volume is carried by the narrator Lockwood, who tells the story of how he moved into the empty Wuthering Heights, and how he was entertained by the reclusive _Heathcliff_ , and then left alone for several weeks and was obliged to escape by a trapdoor. The third volume is narrated by an old man called Joseph, who was a servant in the household when _Heathcliff_ and Catherine were alive, and who is now, of course, old and feeble. He tells the story of the death of Catherine, and the subsequent death of _Heathcliff_ , and then describes how the young people of the household, who are the children of Catherine and _Heathcliff_ , now live together at Wuthering Heights.
It is difficult to see why Walpole thought that this confused and disjointed tale would make a great novel, but it is even more difficult to understand why he thought it was a great poem. _The Cathedral_ is a mess of over-explanatory and tedious verse, and it is not surprising that it has been so little read.

In 1920 , Innis joined the department of political economy at the University of Toronto . He was assigned to teach courses in c

urrency and banking . In 1921 , he became a founding member of the Canadian Institute of International Affairs (CIIA) and was named its first President in 1923 . He later became a director of the Toronto Stock Exchange . In 1934 , he was appointed to the Royal commission on the Banking and Financial System .
In 1936 , Innis and his wife, Lorna, moved to Chicago , Illinois , where he became a professor at the University of Chicago . In 1954, he was elected president of the American Political Science Association .
 Innis' most notable claim to fame was his claim that all historians should be economic historians. He believed that economic historian s should be concerned with the history of human economic institutions , their development and transformation over time and the impact they have on human society . Innis believed that history should be more than just a collection of events.
Lorna Innis was a passionate gardener and a gifted cook. Her cookbook published in 1954, "The Innis Cook Book: A Collection of Recipes from the Dinner Table", was very popular. She was known as a kind and considerate person who helped many people in need. She died in 1971 at the age of 75.
The home where Sir Innis and his family lived from 1926 to 1936 is now designated as a heritage building and part of the Toronto Historical Society.
His son, Michael Innis, is a professor at Western University and author of "The Great Democracy: A History of the American Idea".
 Some of his books were published posthumously.

Skye , or the Isle of Skye ( / skaɪ / ; Scottish Gaelic : An t @-@ Eilean Sgitheanach or Eilean a ' Cheò ) , is the largest and

northernmost island of the Inner Hebrides of Scotland . The island's peninsulas radiate out from a mountainous center dominated by the Cuillin , the rocky slopes of which provide some of the most dramatic mountain scenery in the country. Skye has been occupied since the Mesolithic period, and the first written mention of the island (as Ely) is by the Roman geographer Pomponius Mela, c. 43. The Norse made several short-lived settlements on the island, and from the 13th century the Clan MacLeod ruled. Skye is connected to the mainland by the Skye Bridge, and ferries sail from Armadale on the Isle of Skye to Mallaig on the mainland (Lochalsh ); there are also ferries from Uig on the Isle of Skye to Tarbert on Harris in the Outer Hebrides.

Three of the small vessels managed to return to England : MLs 160 , 307 and 443 . They had reached the rendezvous and waited un

successfully for the rest of the convoy. The three MLs had been built at the beginning of the war to carry troops to Norway. They were now used as auxiliary patrol vessels. ML 160 was captained by the affable and eccentric Lieutenant Commander Geoffrey Stevens. The first of the three vessels to rejoin the main convoy, ML 160 was involved in the rescue of two other ships.
The Royal Navy had been keeping a sharp look out for German submarines ever since the war began. It had set up a chain of submarine listening posts along the shoreline of both the east and west coasts and a number of vessels were used to detect the tell-tale noises of submarines. This system was known as Asdic. Asdic was used both by Royal Navy and Allied vessels to detect the presence of submarines. It was this system that had enabled the _Pamir_ to be found.
November 1939 was a particularly cold month and the sea was rough. Because of this the search for the _Pamir_ had to be abandoned. The weather soon improved, however, and the search was resumed. This time the _Pamir_ 's position was pinpointed and it was found that the _Pamir_ had grounded on the Rocks. The Captain of the _Fort Stikine_ , Lieutenant Commander Edward Cunningham, decided that his best chance of saving the _Pamir_ would be to board her. The three remaining MLs were ordered to accompany the _Fort Stikine_ to the scene. When the _Fort Stikine_ was within a mile of the _Pamir_ it was boarded by Lieutenant Commander Stevens and his crew. The _Fort Stikine_ then towed the _Pamir_ to Scapa Flow.
The _Fort Stikine_ was a large American-built freighter that was built in 1918. She was a sturdy vessel of 3,100 tons. She was just over 100 feet long and was 20 feet wide. She had been converted to an Armed Merchant Cruiser, a type of armed merchant ship. Her armament consisted of two 4in guns and three 3in guns. Her original role was to patrol the waters of the Pacific Ocean and she had sailed on many voyages to Japan and China. She was now a convoy escort. The skeleton of the kakapo differs from other parrots in several features associated with flightlessness . Firstly , it has the

largest keel among extant parrots (Figure 1A), which is the structure that connects the breastbone to the sternum. The large keel allows for the attachment of a large breast muscle that is one of the main muscles involved in flight . The kakapo also has a long, slender and elongated sternum (Figure 1A) and a long and narrow pectoral girdle (Figure 1B). The long and narrow pectoral girdle enables the large breast muscle to move the kakapo's body in a unique way, with the sternum acting as a lever . The combination of these features gives the kakapo a unique bipedal locomotor style and enables the bird to run at high speeds and wag its tail like a dog, although the kakapo does not actively wag the tail . These specialized skeletal features are believed to be specifically related to flightlessness.
The kakapo is therefore an example of an evolutionary transition to flightlessness. Therefore , the study of kakapo skeletal biomechanics may provide important clues to the evolutionary transition to flightlessness and also shed light on the evolution of flight.

The family includes Lutheran ministers, one of whom is her father. Fey's mother is of English and Northern Irish ancestry. Her paternal grandfather was born in England and her paternal grandmother in Northern Ireland.
Fey's family moved to Burr Ridge , Illinois , when she was a child. She attended Glenbard West High School in Glen Ellyn , Illinois , where she was a classmate of actress Amy Poehler . Fey joined the drama club, and performed in the musical The Music Man. She was also the manager of the girls' basketball team. Fey graduated from the University of Virginia in 1992 with a Bachelor of Arts degree. While at Virginia, she wrote for the campus newspaper The Cavalier Daily. She was a member of the Kappa Alpha Theta sorority.
During her senior year at the University of Virginia, Fey wrote and performed in a comedy show titled The Virgina Tech Mystery Plays, which she co-wrote with Jeff Richmond and took to the Edinburgh Festival Fringe in Scotland.
After graduation, Fey moved to Chicago, Illinois to pursue a career in comedy. She later moved to New York City in 1997.

She was a writer for Saturday Night Live from 1997 to 2006. She left in 2006 to focus on her film career.
She has won seven Emmy Awards and a Golden Globe Award for her work at SNL.

In 2004, Fey published her first book, Bossypants. The book began as a series of humorous essays written for The New Yorker magazine. The book was released on March 3, 2011, and was a New York Times bestseller. The book was followed by a humorous autobiography Mean Girls in 2004.

World War II had a significant impact on changing family roles . Because of the draft , workers were scarce in many industries

such as agriculture and manufacturing. In addition, many men and women worked in the military .
During the war, Rosie the Riveter became a symbol for women who worked in the factories . At first, the government expected women to work in the factories at home, but as the war progressed , the government realized it needed to employ women. By 1945, more than 350,000 women worked in the war industry .
In 1940, women made up 8 percent of the U.S. labor force , but by 1945, they made up 37 percent of the labor force .
Some women even took jobs in dangerous places, such as shipyards and factories making war materials. Some women even became soldiers, as in the case of the Women's Army Auxiliary Corps .
Even though many women were working outside the home, some still stayed at home to raise children or care for elderly relatives.
By 1945, many families found themselves on wartime rations as food was frequently rationed . Many families had to do with less, but many families were also spared the tragedy of the Great Depression .

About 250 Pictish stones survive and have been assigned by scholars to three classes . Class I stones are those thought to date

from the 5th and 6th centuries AD and contain symbols or carvings related to the Norse Picts, a people of Scandinavian origin who invaded and settled in Scotland and Orkney in the 9th century AD. They may also contain symbols related to the early Picts, a people who settled there in the 4th century AD and whose name comes from the Latin word Picti. Class II stones are those theorized to have been erected during the 10th century, and Class III stones are thought to be the work of 16th- and 17th-century masons who were influenced by the earlier Class I and Class II stones.
I work with wood and stone. I am drawn to the materials for their hardness and resistance to decay. I am fascinated by the evidence of the past and the way that a material can be worked to convey a message that is out of time but that can be read with a certain amount of confidence.
The Pictish stones have always been a source of joy and mystery for me. I have used them as a starting point for many commissions. However, I have decided to take the opportunity of this project to develop my own work based on the stones. I am drawn to the way in which the Picts, in their simplest form, used the stone to record their name and carved a symbol representing their social group or their rank. As I work, I will consider the aesthetic, the formal and the symbolic aspects of the stones, and how I can take these principles into my own work.
The work will be shown at the end of the project.

He had no illusions about the Americanization of Canada, but he thought that the United States was not the only important influence in the world. He believed that Canadians had to reclaim their place in world affairs and not simply follow wherever the United States led. He believed that Canada needed to be strong enough to defend its own interests. But he also believed that Canada had to be strong enough to help other countries. "We have a duty to help to build a peaceful world," he said.
Innis's ideas about Canada's place in the world were rooted in his ideas about economics. In July 1948, at a time when the politicians of all parties in Ottawa were making fools of themselves by declaring that Canadians could never again be allowed to be poor, Innis gave a speech that could have been written to oppose the Conservative government's new welfare state. Bid development[edit]
In the 2002 Olympic Congress , it was decided that the Youth Olympic Games ( YOG ) would be held every four years, alternating with the Winter Olympics. The 2009 Congress also decided that the inaugural Youth Olympics would be held in 2012, and that the YOG would take place four years after each Summer Olympics .[1]
The IOC had considered bidding for the 2012 Summer Youth Olympics , but decided against it. They claimed that it was due to a lack of resources, although a number of countries, including South Africa and Brazil , were interested in hosting the first YOG.[2]
On 29 April , 2006, the IOC Executive Board (EB) approved the candidature of the three cities to host the 2012 Youth Olympic Games: Belgrade , Buenos Aires and Lillehammer .[3] The 119th IOC Session , held in Guatemala City on 6 July , 2007, decided to again approve the candidature of the three cities, and added two more candidates: Riga and Amsterdam .[4]
On 15 May , 2008, the IOC Executive Board suspended the candidature of Lillehammer , due to limited support from local and government authorities.[5] On 28 May , Buenos Aires and Belgrade withdrew their candidatures. The IOC Executive Board decided to select the host city through a vote of the IOC Session in July , 2007, and that the EB would carry out a final evaluation of the two candidates from 17 to 20 June , 2007.[6]
On 14 June , 2007, the IOC EB chose Buenos Aires and Amsterdam as the two final candidates. The 119th IOC Session held in Guatemala City on 6 July , 2007, decided to approve the candidature of Buenos Aires and Amsterdam for the 2012 Youth Olympic Games and invited both cities to make a bid for the Games.[7]
On 10 June , 2009, the IOC Executive Board approved the candidature of the three cities to host the 2014 Youth Olympic Games: Rappi, Almaty and Stockholm .[8] The 121st IOC Session , held in Copenhagen on 31 October , 2009, decided to select the host city through a vote of the IOC Session, and that the EB would carry out a final evaluation of the three candidates from 22 to 23 October .[9]

The Amps were an American alternative @-@ indie rock group . Formed by Kim Deal in 1995 after her band the Breeders went on hia

-@-@ hiatus, the Amps were signed to K Records. They released their debut single "Pacer" in 1996, and their debut album Gala Mill the following year. The Amps' second and final album, Trash Talkers , was released in 1999.
The Amps were initially formed in 1995 by Kim Deal (bass, vocals) and Tobi Vail (drums). Deal and Vail were both members of the Breeders. Deal was inspired to form the Amps after the Breeders disbanded in 1990, and her mother passed away in 1994. Deal recruited Shannon Drew (guitar) and Christopher Monger (keyboards) to the group, and the lineup was complete.
The Amps released their debut single "Pacer" in 1996, which was also the title track of their 1996 EP. In 1997, Nirvana's Kurt Cobain's mother, Wendy O'Connor, paid for the Amps to record their debut album Gala Mill. The group signed to K Records that same year.
The Amps released their debut album Gala Mill on 16 March 1998. The album was produced by Steve Albini, and the group was reportedly unhappy with the album's recording. A limited edition 7" vinyl single of "Three is a Magic Number" was released. The group disbanded in 1999.
In 1999, the Amps released their second and final album, Trash Talkers . The group was signed by the American label, Geffen Records. The album was produced by Steve Albini, and the group was reportedly unhappy with the album's recording. The album was met with poor reviews, and the group disbanded shortly after its release.
The Amps' first two albums were released by K Records, and their third album was released by Geffen Records.
The outbreak of the Civil War shook public confidence in the Union , and citizens began hoarding specie , gold and silver coins

, as well as Confederate currency . Even after the war ended, the public's confidence in the federal government's ability to provide financial security was shaken, and in the early 1870s, the nation's economy was in turmoil. The country had borrowed heavily to finance the war, and with interest payments and other obligations, the national debt was overwhelming.
It was during this period of economic crisis that Congress adopted the Coinage Act of 1873, which effectively ended the free coinage of silver. The act, which was signed into law by President Ulysses S. Grant on February 12, 1873, provided that no more silver could be coined into United States coins beyond the amount required to pay the national debt as it was contracted in 1873. This amounted to about 15 million troy ounces of silver per annum. The act also specified that the melt value of each dollar in gold coinage had to be 0.900 fine.
The act was passed as a means of stabilizing the nation's currency and reducing the debt. Even so, the measure had the effect of decreasing the amount of silver available to the public, which was one of its intended effects.
The act also established the first gold reserve requirement, which required that the amount of silver mined could not exceed the amount of gold coined into the nation's currency. On the other hand, the act also established a bullion dealer's license and prohibited the manufacture and issuance of private coinage.
There was, of course, a great deal of controversy over the act, which was passed by a narrow margin in Congress. However, the act remained in effect for the next 25 years.
The outbreak of the Spanish-American War in April of 1898 resulted in a renewed demand for silver as an alternative to gold. Congress responded to this demand by adopting the Sherman Silver Purchase Act, which was signed into law on May 15, 1890. The act required the Treasury to purchase between two and four million ounces of silver per month and was intended to increase the amount of silver mined.
The act resulted in an increase in the amount of silver mined, but this amount was still insufficient to meet the required monthly purchase requirement. Congress responded to this by adopting the Bland-Allison Act on February 28, 1878, which provided that the Treasury was required to purchase between 2 and 4 million ounces of silver per month. The act required the Treasury to purchase the silver from private mining companies.
The Act also established a bullion dealer's license, which was required for any person or corporation that was engaged in the purchase or sale of bullion.
The Bland-Allison Act remained in effect until 1900, when Congress passed the Gold Standard Act, which restored the gold standard to the nation. As a result of the act, the Treasury was no longer required to purchase silver for coinage.
The Sherman Silver Purchase Act and the Bland-Allison Act were both passed during the administration of President Benjamin Harrison. The passage of these acts marked the beginning of the end for silver as a legal tender in the United States.

Aretusa was a torpedo cruiser of the Partenope class built for the Italian Regia Marina ( Royal Navy ) in the 1880s . Laid down

in 1882 , she was launched in 1884 and commissioned into the Italian fleet in 1887 .
Assigned to the Submarine Minesweeper Division in the Mediterranean , Aretusa took part in the Italo-Ethiopian War of 1895–96 , during which she was used as a transport ship . She was decommissioned in 1896 and sold to the French Navy in 1902 .
She was then converted into a training ship and served in this capacity until 1912 . Aretusa was decommissioned for the second time in 1915 and sold for scrap in 1918 .
The ship was named after the mythical river Aretusa , which flows between the regions of Sicily and Calabria .
Aretusa was 68.08 meters (223 ft 7 in) long overall and had a beam of 7.40 m (24 ft 3 in) and a draft of 2.66 m (8 ft 8 in). She displaced 943 long tons (958 t) at normal load and 1,220 long tons (1,240 t) at full load .
She was powered by a single-cylinder expansion steam engine that drove a single screw propeller. The engine was rated at 3,940 horsepower (2,940 kW), giving Aretusa a top speed of 19 knots (35 km / h; 22 mph). She had a maximum range of 4,398 nautical miles (8,180 km; 5,086 mi) at 10 knots (19 km / h; 12 mph). Her crew consisted of 99 officers and sailors.
Aretusa was armed with two 5.9-inch (150 mm) 54-caliber guns and two 47 mm (1.85 in) Hotchkiss revolver cannons. She also had three 356 mm (14 in) torpedo tubes, all of them in the bow.
Aretusa was laid down at the Castellammare shipyard on April 20, 1882 and launched on June 30, 1884 . She was completed on October 29, 1887 .
Aretusa was assigned to the Submarine Minesweeper Division in the Mediterranean and took part in the Italo-Ethiopian War of 1895–96 . She was used as a transport ship to the island of Pantelleria .
With the outbreak of the First World War , Aretusa was decommissioned on July 31, 1915 . She was decommissioned for the second time on September 2, 1918 and subsequently sold for scrap . She was scrapped in 1921.

Currently , Paranthodon is classified as a stegosaurus related to Stegosaurus , Tuojiangosaurus , and Loricatosaurus . However

while the name is still under review , there is a proposal to merge the genus in the genus Stegosaurus .
The genus Paranthodon was named in 1989 by paleontologist Peter Galton , based on remains discovered in the Early Jurassic (Sinemurian) Upper Lias formation of Lyme Regis , England . Galton based the genus name on the Greek words παρα (para) which means "near" and ἃνθος (anthos) which means "flower" . The genus name was chosen to reflect the "nearness" of the species to Stegosaurus . The species name, parthenon , is a reference to the Parthenon .
Galton described most of the known material as belonging to a single species , including 12 specimens from the Lyme Regis area, and compared it to Stegosaurus . Galton suggested that the material from Lyme Regis was probably contemporaneous with Stegosaurus from the Morrison Formation of North America .
The type species Paranthodon lymeregiensis was described in 1989 by paleontologist Peter Galton .
Two other species were later named in the genus , Paranthodon gracilis in 1989 by paleontologist Peter Galton , and Paranthodon cromptoni in 2004 by paleontologist Robert Smith .
Paranthodon lymeregiensis  is the type species of the genus Paranthodon . Based on a skull fragment, a right dentary, three caudal vertebrae, and a partial sacrum , Galton determined that it was a basal stegosaur . Galton assigned it to Stegosauridae based on its similarities to Stegosaurus . He noted that the species was further supported by similarities to Tuojiangosaurus and Loricatosaurus . It is currently the only member of the genus Paranthodon .
Paranthodon gracilis  is the only species of the genus Paranthodon from the Sinemurian of England . Based on a partial skull , Galton assigned it to its own monotypic genus in 1989, based on its similarity to Stegosaurus , but noted that the species was further supported by similarities to Tuojiangosaurus and Loricatosaurus .
Paranthodon cromptoni  is a stegosaur from the Early Jurassic (Sinemurian) Upper Lias formation of Lyme Regis , England . Based on a partial skull , Galton assigned it to its own monotypic genus in 1989, based on its similarity to Stegosaurus , but noted that the species was further supported by similarities to Tuojiangosaurus and Loricatosaurus .

Little is known of the circumstances under which the mosaics were made, and there is no documentary evidence to help us reconstruct the events. We know that an inscription on the panel in the Museu Nacional in Rio de Janeiro (Fig. 3.1) reads 'Made by order of Hadrian', and that is the only clue we have to the date. The panel in the Louvre is also dated 'AD 121' but on the basis of its subject matter. We can only guess at the circumstances in which the mosaics were made. The inscriptions, if they are genuine, are the only indication that they were commissioned by an individual. The lack of any other indication is not surprising. The mosaics were made in a workshop, and the workshop would have been the commissioner. The mosaics represent the work of the workshop, not of the commissioner, and the commissioner would have had no interest in advertising his work. He would have had no need to do so. The mosaics would have been his main business.
But who was the commissioner? The first place to look is the subject matter of the panels. If the subject matter is of no help, we have to look elsewhere. The best way to begin this is to give a brief account of the more interesting panels.
3.1 The mosaic in the Museu Nacional, Rio de Janeiro
This is the only one of the three panels which is dated. The inscription reads: 'Hadrian the emperor made them'. The subject is a triumphant procession, which is very different from the other two. The procession is led by four elephants and four chariots, with a group of mounted officers following on horseback. In the distance is a large group of civilians, with a second group of mounted officers. This is followed by a third group, consisting of two elephants, two chariots, and a cavalry unit. All the subjects are in armour.
The artist has a real sense of movement and excitement. The horses are galloping. The elephants are moving with a real sense of forward momentum. The subjects are well composed, with characters and objects leading the eye to the next.
The landscape is attractive enough to be considered a separate subject, and it is perhaps the most difficult part of the mosaic to understand. But the artist has made it more difficult by the frequent insertion of subjects and objects which have no relevance to the triumph. These are the Roman fasces, a group of prisoners, a large sailing vessel, and a group of horsemen. We do not know what the artist had in mind when he inserted some of these subjects, and we do not know whether they are supposed to be part of the triumph.
The mosaic is in the Museu Nacional in Rio de Janeiro. It was discovered in 1900 in the Carioca Valley in the State of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, but it is not known when it was placed there. It was taken from the valley floor by the Brazilian Government and was bought by the French Government in 1903. It was shipped to France and installed in the Louvre, where it was exhibited in 1904. It was bought by the French Government and installed in the Museu Nacional in 1908.
The mosaic is 1.42 metres high and 2.87 metres wide. It was made by inlaying the design on a white background and then inlaying the pebbles. The pebbles were cut from the local rock, which was a white limestone.
The mosaic is in a fair condition. The pebbles are well fitted and the surface is smooth. Some of the pebbles are missing. The damage is probably recent and is probably due to the fact that the mosaic was moved.

In addition to the eight named storms of 1973 and two notable tropical depressions , there were several minor systems that were

monitored by the National Hurricane Center over the course of that year.
Tropical Storm Alma developed on October 12 near the Cape Verde Islands. The storm tracked northwestward across the Atlantic, passing to the west of the Cape Verde Islands on the 15th. Alma was a tropical storm at its peak, with winds of 70 mph (110 km/h) and a minimum pressure of 982 mbar (hPa; 29.0 inHg), and it was the first storm to be named by the National Hurricane Center in 1973. The storm was dissipated by the time it reached the latitude of the Azores on the 17th.
Tropical Storm Babs was a short-lived tropical cyclone that formed in the eastern Caribbean Sea on September 13, 1973. The storm tracked northwestward, passing to the west of Puerto Rico on September 15. Babs quickly weakened into a tropical depression on the 16th and dissipated later that day.
Tropical Depression Three was a short-lived tropical cyclone that formed in the western Caribbean Sea on September 13, 1973. The storm tracked northwestward, passing to the west of Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula on the 15th. The depression dissipated later that day over the Yucatán Peninsula.
Tropical Depression Four was a short-lived tropical cyclone that formed in the western Caribbean Sea on September 15, 1973. The depression tracked northwestward, passing to the west of Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula on the 16th. The depression dissipated later that day over the Yucatán Peninsula.

Tropical Depression Ten was a short-lived tropical cyclone that formed in the western Caribbean Sea on October 1, 1973. The depression tracked northwestward, passing to the west of Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula on the 3rd. The depression dissipated later that day over the Yucatán Peninsula.
Tropical Depression Eleven was a short-lived tropical cyclone that formed in the western Caribbean Sea on October 7, 1973. The depression tracked northwestward, passing to the west of Mexico's Yucatán Peninsula on the 8th. The depression dissipated later that day over the Yucatán Peninsula.

In the early 1950s , working in Hanford and Savannah River Sites , Reines and Cowan developed the equipment and procedures with

which they observed the natural processes of nuclear beta decay to confirm and extend the work of Enrico Fermi, Bruno Pontecorvo, Emilio Segre, and others . In 1957, Cowan, Reines, and other scientists observed the first free neutrinos to confirm Pontecorvo's predictions of the existence of neutrinos. These experiments were the first to detect antineutrinos and confirmed the predictions of Pontecorvo's unified weak interaction theory .
 The discovery of the neutrino confirmed that the weak force was responsible for nuclear beta decay (in which a neutron decays into a proton and an electron or positron) as well as for the emission of other particles in the decay of certain unstable atomic nuclei. It was a key step in the development of the Standard Model of particle physics .
In 1940, Clyde Cowan received a Bachelor of Science degree from Yale University in physics. In 1942, he began research in nuclear physics at Columbia University under the guidance of Enrico Fermi. In 1943, he was drafted into the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, where he worked at the Army's Los Alamos Scientific Laboratory as a member of the Theoretical Physics Group under J. Robert Oppenheimer.
While at Los Alamos, Cowan worked on the Manhattan Project to develop the atomic bomb. In particular, he designed and built a critical mass of uranium that could be used in an atomic bomb. In 1946, Cowan was awarded the Medal for Merit .

## Plot

The story of Mega Man & Bass varies slightly depending on which player character is chosen. It begins One year after Mega Man 8 and several years after Mega Man and Mega Man 2. Mega Man and Bass both end up in the same place after a battle with Bass. One day, Mega Man recieves a message from Dr. Light. It tells him that a robotic creature, known as "Dr. Wily's Weapon", has been attacking the Wily castle. Mega Man and Bass both go to investigate, only to find no trace of the Weapon. On the way home, Mega Man is attacked by the Weapon and is sent into a huge canyon. Bass, after hearing of these events, decides to take a peek. He also finds the Weapon and is sent into the same canyon. After both are sent to the canyon, the Weapon is destroyed by an unknown force. Mega Man and Bass then find each other and go to the city. A year after this, they are attacked by a mysterious figure and are sent into the Deadly Silence stage.

### The Giant MG

With Bass in full control of Dr. Wily's castle, Mega Man is forced to use any means necessary to defeat him.

In the final battle, Mega Man is forced to use any means necessary to beat Bass. When Mega Man is knocked down, Bass picks him up and prepares to deliver the killing blow. Mega Man suddenly realizes that, through the assistance of Dr. Light, he has the ability to bestow his powers onto Bass. Mega Man then uses this ability on Bass, fusing the two Robot Masters into one.

Bass, now possessed of Mega Man's powers, declares himself "The Giant MG" and engulfs the entire castle in a fireball. In the end, Mega Man is able to destroy Bass, but not before he is knocked down again and is unable to stop Bass from destroying the castle. After the castle's destruction, Bass is thought to have been killed and Mega Man is declared a hero.

## Development

Mega Man & Bass is a spin-off of the previous Mega Man X series, which had been developed by Capcom for the Super Famicom in Japan. Mega Man & Bass was the final title released in the Mega Man series for the Super Famicom, and was the first in the series to be developed in-house by Capcom. Mega Man & Bass was released in Japan on December 12, 1998, in the United States on April 1, 1999, and in Europe on October 1, 1999. The game was developed by a team of four people, led by Masahiro Yuge.

The game's development started in late 1996, and the project had gone through 18 iterations before it was released. The game was originally planned to be titled Mega Man Xtreme, and was going to be a compilation of Mega Man X and Mega Man X2. However, the development team found it difficult to bring the games to the Super Famicom, and decided to rework them into a new game.

The team had also planned to use a new character, named Jet, who was to be the main character of the game. However, the team chose to use the main characters of the Mega Man X series, Mega Man and Bass, instead due to the existing popularity of the characters. The team also chose to use the characters due to the existing fanbase of Mega Man X in Japan.
