# **16. WOOD SUPPLY, BRAZOS GAP, 1875**
In 1875, the Brazos Gap Company of Texas was formed to purchase timber from Brazos Gap (now Lake Granbury) and transport it to the mouth of the Brazos River for shipment to customers in the East.
In the spring of 1875, a large sawmill was erected at Brazos Gap, and a railroad was constructed to carry logs to the mill. By the end of the year, some $500,000 worth of logs had been cut and shipped.
Prior to this project, the Brazos Gap Company had been unable to export enough logs to cover its costs of operation. But, with the new sawmill, the company could produce enough sawed lumber to sell at a profit.
Resources
Bailey, William C. The History of Texas. Austin: University of Texas Press, 1969.
# **17. BRAZOS RIVER STEAMBOATS, 1850–1861**
Steamboats began operating on the Brazos River in the 1850s. By 1856, the _Charles Thompson,_ a four-masted screwboat, was transporting cotton from Houston to the Brazos River, where it was loaded onto steamboats for transport to New Orleans.
Some of the Brazos River steamboats that operated during the Civil War were the _Fannie,_ the _Dorothy,_ and the _Billie._
The first railroad in Texas was the Houston and Texas Central Railroad, which was built to carry cotton from Houston to the Brazos River.
During the Civil War, the Texas coast was blockaded by Union ships. Cotton from Houston could be shipped only by way of the Brazos River.
Resources
Bosch, Martin. _History of Texas._ 4th ed. New York: American Historical Society, 1915.
# **18. BRAZOS RIVER STEAMBOATS, 1866–1869**
In 1866, the first passenger steamboat left Houston for a landing on the Brazos River.
In 1867, the _Brazos,_ a 200-ton side-wheeler, was launched at Houston. The _Brazos_ was the first steamboat to successfully navigate the Brazos River to the Gulf of Mexico.
Resources
Bosch, Martin. _History of Texas._ 4th ed. New York: American Historical Society, 1915.
# **19. BRAZOS PORTS, 1850–1853**
Between 1850 and 1853, three ports were established on the Brazos River:
  * Brazos Landing, a port located 12 miles upstream from the mouth of the Brazos River.
  * Brazos City, a port located at the mouth of the Brazos River.
  * West Columbia, a port located 5 miles upstream from the mouth of the Brazos River.
In 1853, the Brazos Landing was renamed Brazoria, and West Columbia was renamed Columbia.

During the same time frame as the Hitchcock rumors , goaltender Curtis Sanford returned from his groin injury on November 13 .

He started in a game against the Washington Capitals , but the Canucks lost 5–4 in overtime.  Sanford suffered a concussion in that game which caused him to miss the next two games. He returned to the lineup on November 19.
Following the Hitchcock rumors, the Vancouver Canucks announced that their team had the worst record (4–11–4) in the Western Conference.  The Canucks were also in last place in the Pacific Division, three points behind the Calgary Flames.  They were tied with the Dallas Stars and the Washington Capitals for the worst record in the league.  They were in last place in the NHL with 12 points.
The Canucks' poor performance was due to their offense.  They had scored only 28 goals so far, which was the lowest scoring team in the NHL.
The general manager of the Canucks, Dave Nonis, commented on the Hitchcock rumors after the game.  He said, "I don't know where that started. I don't know how it got out. I don't know why people are so interested in Ken Hitchcock. There's a lot of teams out there with some big-name coaches, but they're not winning.  I'm not sure where the story came from, but I'm not going to comment on it."
Although the Canucks were not doing well, Nonis said, "We've gone through this before. I think some of our players realize what's going on and they can get going. We've been through this before and we're going to get through it again. We're going to get through it again and have a very good team here. We're going to do it."
Ian Gordon, a sports columnist for the Vancouver Province and the Vancouver Sun, wrote on November 15 that during the Hitchcock rumors, the Canucks were playing some of the worst hockey in the league.  He questioned why the Canucks' owners, Francesco Aquilini and the Aquilini Investment Group, would want to fire Hitchcock.
Gordon argued that Hitchcock had done a good job with the team.  He said, "It's hard to argue that Hitchcock isn't a good coach, considering he's taken the Canucks to the playoffs five times in six years. Yes, they were ousted in the first round every year, but that didn't stop the Canucks from giving Hitchcock a four-year contract extension last summer."
Gordon also said that Hitchcock was responsible for the Canucks' offense.  He added that "Hitchcock is a defensive coach, but he's also made it clear that he doesn't want the Canucks to be a one-dimensional team. 'I'm not the kind of coach that says, 'This is the way I coach and this is the way we're going to play,' ' Hitchcock said."
Gordon commented on the fact that the Canucks had a good record (10–5–4) in the previous 19 games.  He wrote, "Hitchcock's record in the previous 19 games is 10–5–4. That's a winning record, whether you think that's good enough to keep the job or not. If Hitchcock goes, the Canucks will find another coach, but it's hard to argue that the Canucks still wouldn't be a better team than the one they have right now."
Hitchcock continued to coach the Canucks through the end of the 2006–07 season.  They finished with a record of 37–35–10, which was good enough to qualify for the playoffs.  However, they lost in the first round to the Edmonton Oilers.
As the Canucks' poor record continued in the 2007–08 season, rumors of Hitchcock's possible departure increased.  On November 15, 2007, the Canucks announced that they had placed Hitchcock on administrative leave.  The Canucks also announced that general manager Dave Nonis would be the head coach for the remainder of the season.  Nonis had been the general manager of the Canucks since 2003. Verpa bohemica is a species of fungus in the family Morchellaceae . Commonly known as the early morel ( or early false morel )

it can be found growing in early spring in central and eastern Europe and Asia Minor . This species is a mycophagous parasite that grows in association with the roots of birch trees . It is similar in appearance to Morchella esculenta ( the true morel )  and was once thought to be a species of Morchella. 

## Taxonomy

This species was first described scientifically by famed French naturalist Pierre Bulliard in 1790. It was placed in the genus Verpa by German mycologist Curt Romstorff in 1942. Swedish mycologist Karin Britt Ekman re-classified it under the genus Morchella in 2000 .

## Description

Verpa bohemica is characterized by the presence of a gleba ( the mass of spores that develops inside the cap of the mushroom ) that is whitish in color and has a fleshy texture. The hymenophore is made up of multiple, densely packed pilei ( the clusters of tissue that produce spores ) that are white in color. The mushroom has a nondescript odor and flavor.

## Habitat and distribution

This species is found in central and eastern Europe and Asia Minor  and grows in early spring in association with birch trees . It forms ectomycorrhizal associations with birches .

on of Dr. Markus Flück (Switzerland). The name was published in 2005 by Josef Breitenbach and Karl Hausko. The fungus is active during the autumn season. Assay for Antimony
Synthesis of Antimony-121
121Sb can be synthesized by β-decay of 123Te, which has a half-life of 35 hours. The preparation of 123Te involves a spontaneous fission reaction and is a two-step process. An electron accelerator is used to bombard a cesium-133 target with 5.9 MeV electrons. The target is in a vacuum tank and is moderated by liquid deuterium. The accelerated electrons are stopped in the target, producing a large number of deuterons. The deuterons are captured by the cesium-133, thereby forming the 123Te isotope. The 123Te decays to 121Sb with a β− decay of 123Te (half-life = 35 hours).
Decay of 121Sb
121Sb has a β− decay to 121I (half-life = 2.5 minutes). The β− decay energy is 616.9 keV. The β− particle is a high-energy electron, which is emitted from the nucleus of the 121Sb atom.
Artificial 125Sb can be prepared by proton bombardment of 124Sb. The half-life of this isotope is 11.4 days and the decay mode is by β− decay to 125Te.
Use of Antimony in Medicine
Because of the high β− activity of 121Sb, it is used as a radiopharmaceutical in cardiac imaging (Ga-68). The Ga-68 emits β− particles with a 511 keV energy and is used to detect coronary arterial disease.
Use of Antimony in Industry
Antimony is used in the manufacture of flame retardants, semiconductors, lead-acid storage batteries, alloys, metal casting, pesticides, paints, glass and ceramics.

Although not born in Germany, Reines embraced the German culture, and throughout his career he spoke German and taught the language to his students ( Bauer 1999 ). Reines later said that his romantic interest in physics was fueled by the works of Einstein, and his interest in science was fostered by his chemistry-teacher father ( Reines 1995 , 20).
Reines received a BS in 1940 from the University of California at Los Angeles ( UCLA ) and an MS in 1942 from the University of California at Berkeley . In the war years, Reines worked as a supervisor of instrumentation for the Navy's S-1 program, which was responsible for the construction of the atomic bombs that were dropped on Japan at the end of World War II. In 1946, Reines entered the graduate program at UCLA, where he worked with J. Robert Oppenheimer on gamma ray spectroscopy. He received his PhD in 1948.
In the 1950s, Reines worked with Oppenheimer and Luis Alvarez at the University of California at Berkeley on the experiment that confirmed the existence of the weak force. For this work, Reines received the National Academy of Sciences Public Welfare Medal in 1960 and the Nobel Prize for Physics in 1962.

In the 1950s, scientists understood that the neutrino was the second most abundant particle in the universe. Neutrinos are produced in the sun and in nuclear reactors, and they are released in mega-tonnage when an atom splits. Yet they pass through matter unimpeded. They are like ghosts, invisible to all but their most sensitive detectors.
The neutrino was first observed in 1956, when the physicist Frederick Reines discovered it while researching the solar neutrino problem.
In 1956, Reines and Clyde Wiegand began an experiment to observe the neutrinos produced in the sun. They used a nuclear reactor to produce neutrinos and then detected these particles with a 25,000-liter tank of water. However, the detector did not seem to be working, and Reines and Wiegand concluded that they had no evidence that the neutrinos from the sun had reached the Earth.
In 1958, Reines went to Berkeley, where he began to study the nature of the neutrino. He asked his friend, Luis Alvarez, to help him understand the problems that were plaguing his experiment.
"Frederick was a wonderful colleague, a lovely man, and a great scientist," said Alvarez. "He was a great teacher, too. I learned from him how to do physics."
Alvarez was the first to propose an explanation for Reines's problem. He told Reines that he should remove the air from his tank of water and replace it with liquid Freon. This gas would not conduct electricity, and it would also not absorb neutrinos.

Illinois served with the European Squadron from 1902 to 1903 , and with the North Atlantic Fleet until 1907 , by which time it

had been renamed Illinois (BB-7).

## Service history

Illinois was launched on 6 June 1898, sponsored by Miss E. C. Gill, daughter of Governor Orville H. Brown of Illinois. She was commissioned at the Philadelphia Navy Yard on 2 September 1899, Captain Albert Gleaves in command.

### Spanish–American War

The battleship left Philadelphia on 20 September 1899, bound for the Mediterranean Sea. She arrived at Gibraltar on 27 October, where she embarked the British Royal Marine Artillery.

On 13 November, Illinois arrived at Malta and was assigned to the North Atlantic Squadron. She sailed for the Azores on 23 November, and arrived at Ponta Delgada, São Miguel Island on 28 November. Captain Raymond A. Spruance relieved Captain Gleaves on 1 December.

Illinois arrived off Santiago de Cuba on 24 December and commenced bombarding the city on the 27th. She continued her bombardment off Cuba until 3 January 1900, when she was relieved and sailed for Guantánamo Bay. On 6 January she steamed for Key West, Florida, where she arrived on the 12th.

Illinois arrived at Philadelphia on 23 January 1900, and decommissioned on 24 March. She was placed in reserve at Philadelphia, and recommissioned on 1 July 1900.

The battleship was placed in full commission on 13 September 1900, and sailed for St. Thomas, Virgin Islands, arriving on 20 September. She was placed in ordinary on 30 September 1900.

Illinois was recommissioned on 14 May 1901, and sailed for Key West on 28 May. She returned to Philadelphia on 11 June and decommissioned on 30 July.

### Post-Spanish–American War

Illinois recommissioned on 20 September 1901, and sailed for New Orleans, Louisiana, arriving on 1 October. She decommissioned again on 16 October and was placed in reserve. On 19 February 1902 she was placed in full commission, Captain Charles W. Todd in command.

She sailed for Europe on 28 March 1902, and arrived at Plymouth, England, on 25 April. She operated with the European Squadron until 23 May 1903, when she got underway for the United States. She arrived at New York City on 2 June.

Illinois was decommissioned on 16 June 1903 and placed in reserve.

### North Atlantic Squadron

Illinois was recommissioned on 17 April 1904, and sailed for the Panama Canal Zone on 12 June. While en route, she steamed to the aid of the steamer Camden, which was in distress off Cape Hatteras, North Carolina. Illinois rescued 23 of the 27 persons aboard Camden.

Illinois arrived at Colón, Panama, on 21 June and operated with the Atlantic Fleet until 17 May 1905, when she steamed for the United States. She arrived at Hampton Roads, Virginia, on 1 June.

She was decommissioned on 7 June 1905 and placed in reserve. She was reclassified as a second-class battleship on 17 July 1905.

Illinois was recommissioned on 28 March 1906, and sailed for the Caribbean on 10 April. She returned to Philadelphia on 12 June and was decommissioned on 14 June.

She was reclassified as a first-class battleship on 1 February 1907.

### North Atlantic Fleet

Illinois was again recommissioned on 11 November 1907, and sailed for the Caribbean on 14 December. She returned to Philadelphia on 10 February 1908 and was decommissioned on 17 February.

The first symptoms of poisoning are the same as those of overdosage of any toadstool. These include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, fever, muscular spasms, and delirium.
The first symptoms of poisoning are the same as those of overdosage of any toadstool. These include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, fever, muscular spasms, and delirium.
The most important characteristic of poisoning is the development of unconsciousness, with slow, irregular breathing and a body temperature of 99 to 106 F. The skin appears yellowish to green, the eyes are sunken, and there is a rash over the abdomen. The gums are so swollen that the teeth are visible through them.
The pulse rate often is the same as that of the temperature, and there is a tendency toward profuse sweating. The abdomen is distended, and there is a tendency toward diarrhea and constipation. The patient dies after a period of 1 to 2 days.
There is no specific treatment for this poisoning. In the early stages, the patient should be kept cool and free of disturbances. The gastric contents should be removed and the patient placed on a laxative diet. Antibiotics should be administered, and a fluid diet should be given. If there is an apparent response, the patient should be kept under observation for another 24 hours.
If the patient becomes unconscious, artificial respiration should be started and maintained until the pulse and respiration are regular. It is very important to maintain the patient's body temperature at 98.6 F. The skin should be bathed frequently with warm water. If the body temperature is allowed to rise above 103.5 F, the patient will develop convulsions. In addition to the antibiotics, the patient should be given a stimulant.

Palace Software , the developer of the two Barbarian games , marketed the sequel with the same strategy they used for the first

game: a sales pitch with a promise of more violence and more blood. The introduction of the game showed a beheading and a zombie eating its victim’s heart. The top of the package showed a close up of a decapitated head.

## Gameplay

The game plays similarly to the first game, with the addition of the ability to equip a shield. The player must fight through 14 rooms on a single level. Each room contains one or more enemies, and when the room is cleared, it moves on to the next and so on. There are basic enemies such as skeletons and slimes, but there are also more dangerous foes like ghouls, zombies, and even spiders.

## Reception

Reception

Review scores

The game received mixed reviews. The game received praise for its graphics and sound but was criticized for having repetitive gameplay and lack of innovation. Computer Gaming World in 1990 criticized the game for being similar to the first Barbarian , but said that "there is an excellent game here. If you liked the original, you'll like this one; if you didn't like the first one, you probably won't like this one."

The total complement of proteins present at a time in a cell or cell type is known as its proteome , and the study of such larg

escale proteomes is known as proteomics . The proteomics of cellular compartments can be used to monitor the state of a cell or cell type during disease or in response to drug treatment, and also to investigate the mechanisms through which the proteome changes as a cell undergoes proliferation, differentiation or apoptosis.
The proteomes of the various cellular compartments have been studied through proteomic approaches such as two-dimensional polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (2D-PAGE), two-dimensional liquid chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry (2D LC-MS/MS), liquid chromatography coupled to tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS), capillary isoelectric focusing (cIEF) and multidimensional protein identification technology (MudPIT).
The proteome of the outer cell membrane also contains proteins from the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), Golgi apparatus and cytosol that have been ‘targeted' to the plasma membrane by a lipid anchor. The plasma membrane also contains transmembrane proteins that are able to span the membrane.
The ER is the major site of protein synthesis in the cell and contains a large repertoire of proteins, including ribosomal proteins, chaperones, folding enzymes and glycoproteins.
The Golgi apparatus is responsible for the sorting and processing of proteins synthesized in the ER. While proteins synthesized in the ER must be reduced and carboxylated to be able to fold properly, they are also glycosylated in the Golgi apparatus to form complex glycoproteins and proteoglycans.
The endoplasmic reticulum (ER), Golgi apparatus and plasma membrane are enclosed by a lipid bilayer . Lipids in the cell membrane include a variety of fats (triglycerides, phospholipids and steroids), waxes and steroids. Phospholipids are important as they form the outer layer of the cell membrane and are also important for the regulation of protein folding and trafficking.
The outer cell membrane is a dynamic membrane that is constantly being renewed by the ER, Golgi apparatus and plasma membrane. The appearance of the outer cell membrane is constantly changing due to the addition and removal of proteins from the outer cell membrane.
In addition to the proteins that are synthesized and inserted into the outer cell membrane, the outer cell membrane also contains proteins that are transferred from cellular organelles such as the ER, Golgi apparatus and plasma membrane.
The outer cell membrane is also the site of the formation of a variety of cell-surface receptors, signaling molecules and enzymes, which are important for the control of cell proliferation, differentiation and the response to external stimuli.
The outer cell membrane can also form tight junctions and gap junctions that are important for cell-cell and cell-matrix interactions, respectively.
The outer cell membrane can also form desmosomes and hemidesmosomes that are important for cell-cell and cell-matrix interactions, respectively.
As the outer cell membrane is a dynamic membrane that is constantly being renewed, proteins that are synthesized in the ER, Golgi apparatus and plasma membrane and proteins that are transferred from organelles such as the ER, Golgi apparatus and plasma membrane to the outer cell membrane are constantly being removed from the outer cell membrane and replaced with new proteins.

ypassing the rule requiring that they live with the Hudson's Bay Company , they set up what they hoped would become a permanent settlement in present-day southern Alberta . The camp, which they called St. Andrews, was situated on the east bank of the Bow River . In the 1840s, the North West Company , facing competition from the Hudson's Bay Company, sent a group of French Canadians to settle near the new town . In 1846, the North West Company merged with the Hudson's Bay Company, and the new company had the option of taking over the St. Andrews settlement. In 1847 the Hudson's Bay Company formed the Columbia District , which included the St. Andrews settlement; it was renamed Fort Calgary the same year.
Fort Calgary was situated on land owned by NWC and HBC. In 1848, Alexander Loudon, an HBC employee, was sent to establish a trading post at the fort. The post was named Fort Brisebois after Henry Brisebois, the local HBC chief factor , and was located on the west side of the Bow River.
The fort was nothing more than a trading post in 1848. In the following year, a number of American traders and trappers came to Fort Brisebois for supplies. They included Henry and John Augustus Warren, who had been employed by the American Fur Company . After a time, the Warrens moved farther upstream and established Fort Walsh.
In 1850, Edmonton House was built on the Bow River, northwest of Fort Brisebois. Edmund James Neill , an HBC employee, established the post to provide supplies for other companies. That year, the fort had a population of about 30, including Neill and his wife and three children.
In 1851, the American Fur Company assumed management of Fort Brisebois. It was renamed Fort Walsh when the postmaster-general in Ottawa approved the name. The fort had a population of about 100 by that time.
In November 1853, the North West Company and the Hudson's Bay Company signed a joint agreement to develop the fur trade in the area around the fort. That year, Neill received a commission as lieutenant and was appointed chief factor of Fort Walsh.
In 1854, Fort Walsh was the centre of the North West Company's operations in the area. By that time, the NWC had established posts as far north as Edmonton and as far south as the Lesser Slave Lake region.
In 1855, the Hudson's Bay Company assumed full control of Fort Walsh. The post was referred to as Fort Walsh until 1859, when it was renamed Fort Calgary after Calgary Bay, Scotland.
In the 1850s, Fort Calgary became an important centre of the fur trade. The North West Company had its headquarters at the fort. In 1859, the fort had a population of about 350, including 30 or 40 Métis.
In 1855, the North West Company and the Hudson's Bay Company signed a joint agreement to develop the fur trade in the area around the fort. The North West Company continued to operate in the area until 1869, when it was absorbed by the Hudson's Bay Company .
In 1870, the Hudson's Bay Company established a new headquarters for the district in Edmonton. Fort Calgary was reduced to a satellite post.
In 1884, Fort Calgary was the headquarters of the district. In that year, it was listed as a locality in the province of Alberta .
In 1885, the fort fell under the jurisdiction of the North-West Mounted Police. A detachment of the force was established at Fort Calgary the following year.
In 1887, the fort was renamed Fort Brisebois. In that year, the Fort Brisebois detachment of the North-West Mounted Police was amalgamated with the Cochrane detachment and the Fort Macleod detachment to form the Alberta Division of the North-West Mounted Police .
In 1897, Fort Brisebois was the headquarters of the Alberta Division.

D. sulfureus is an entomopathogenic bacterium , which has been used in the biological control of the cocoa pest , the cocoa pod borer , Maruca . toxicology The major toxic effects of D. sulfureus on insects include paralysis and death. The mechanism of action of D. sulfureus involves the disruption of cellular membranes . However, the mechanism by which D. sulfureus produces these toxic effects on insects is unknown. The objective of this work was to determine if D. sulfureus elicits a hypersensitive response (HR) in the black cutworm , Agrotis ipsilon , in order to assess a possible mechanism of action. Methods Black cutworm larvae were exposed to D. sulfureus (109 CFU/mL) and the HR was measured by changes in larval behavior and viability of the cutworms. Results Results showed that D. sulfureus caused a time- and dose-dependent HR in A . ipsilon. Larvae exposed to D. sulfureus (109 CFU/mL) for 60 min exhibited a significant increase in edema and paralysis at 10 min after exposure. At 24 h post-exposure , paralyzed larvae were found in all treatment groups . At 48 h post-exposure , the paralyzed larvae began to die , resulting in 100% mortality of all larvae in all treatment groups compared to control larvae ( P < 0.05). Conclusions D. sulfureus elicits a HR in A . ipsilon larvae. The HR caused by D. sulfureus may be a mechanism of action of this bacterium in insects .

Discovered by Fox et al. in 2002 , paraspeckles are irregularly shaped compartments in the nucleus ' interchromatin space . Fir

estein et al.  reported that paraspeckles do not contain histones, but they are part of the regulated nuclear architecture of the nucleus. They are highly dynamic, fluctuating in size and position, and are thought to be involved in the regulation of gene expression, particularly during the cell cycle. However, the molecular mechanisms by which paraspeckles regulate gene expression are unknown.
Recently, a number of proteins have been found to be involved in the formation of paraspeckles. HMG-coA reductase (HMGCR, also known as 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A reductase, or HMGCR1), which is the rate-limiting enzyme in cholesterol biosynthesis, is one of these proteins. HMGCR interacts with the C-terminal domain of paraspeckle proteins upon mitosis, moves to the nucleolus after mitosis, and is present in the nucleolus in a paraspeckle-like pattern . In mice, HMGCR is required for the formation of paraspeckles and for the regulation of normal cholesterol homeostasis . It is also involved in the regulation of cell cycle progression and the maintenance of chromosome stability . In humans, HMGCR is involved in the regulation of hypoxia-induced angiogenesis .
We previously showed that HMGCR is present in the nucleus . HMGCR not only localizes to the nucleus but also to the nucleolus. The nucleolus is a complex of nuclear substructures that is located in the nucleus and is essential for the formation of ribosomes. In recent years, numerous proteins that are important for ribosome biogenesis have been identified, and hundreds of proteins are now known to be involved in the nucleolus. It has been reported that during mitosis, some proteins in the nucleolus are rapidly degraded, and others are translocated to the nucleus .
In this study, we investigated the subcellular distribution of HMGCR in the interphase nucleus and the mitotic nucleolus, and we examined the relationship between HMGCR and paraspeckles.
Here, we report that the HMGCR protein is present in the nucleus and the nucleolus, and that it is present in paraspeckles. We also show that HMGCR interacts with SFPQ, a protein that forms paraspeckles.

After months of negotiation , John and the envoys from the Latin Empire signed a treaty in Perugia which was confirmed by Pope

Innocent III at the Council of Lyons in 1215.  Despite the treaty , John continued to seek new allies and by 1216 had concluded separate peace treaties with King  Philip II of France and King  Alfonso IX of León . In 1217 , John met with Emperor  Otto IV of the Holy Roman Empire , who had himself been coerced into making a peace treaty with the French, and who was still excommunicated by Innocent III .
 In the spring of 1199 , John's weakness led to a brief period of revolt throughout England . His son ,  Henry , joined in the revolt ,  and his wife ,  Isabella of Gloucester , may have been involved.  The rebels demanded that John retract the provisions of his father's deathbed handover of England to the Holy Roman Empire , and return England to the Crown.  The revolt was put down by John's brother,  Richard I , who had been released from captivity on the continent and was returning to England.  John was forced to accept his father's legacy and to surrender his duchies of Normandy and Aquitaine to his brother,  and to agree to outlaw the use of the name "Lionheart".
 John returned to England ,  and in July 1200 , he married  Isabella of Angoulême ,  a wealthy heiress, in a lavish ceremony in Angoulême . Isabella was the widow of  Hugh X of Lusignan ,  and was the mother of nine-year-old  Aymer Taillefer , who was to inherit Angoulême on her death.  The marriage brought John a large dowry of 100,000 marks in cash ,  plus the considerable Angoulême estate .
 John and Isabella of Angoulême had five children:
  *  Isabella of England (1214–1241)
  *  John of England (1206–1271)
  *  Henry of Almaine (1235–1274)
  *  Eleanor of Provence (1223–1291)
  *  Margaret of England (1240–1275)
John's reign, 1199–1216
As king of England , John was involved in a number of conflicts.  The first concerned the king's brother,  Richard I ,  who had been captured by Leopold V , Duke of Austria , while on his way home from the Third Crusade  . John paid a large ransom for his release in 1194.  The following year, John set out to join the crusade himself, but made poor progress and was captured by Leopold, who in turn surrendered him to Henry VI , Holy Roman Emperor .
The capture of King John by Emperor Henry VI of the Holy Roman Empire in 1198
While John was in captivity in Austria, his brother Richard succeeded him as King of England and left to continue his crusade.  Because of the cost of his ransom, John was forced to surrender the Duchy of Normandy to Philip II of France , and the Duchy of Aquitaine to his brother Richard.  In addition, he was forced to withdraw the support of the English King for the King of France in his dispute with the King of Spain.  John was released from captivity in October 1199 and returned to England.  Upon his return, he was forced to sign the Treaty of Le Goulet , which returned Normandy to French rule, and was also forced to outlaw the use of the term "Lionheart".

Bristow Norway AS is a Norwegian helicopter operator established on 1 May 1985 by Bristow Helicopters UK to operate in the Norwegian market. The company is a subsidiary of Bristow Group, which acquired a 49% shareholding in Bristow Norway in 2008. The company has its head office on Fornebu Flyplass in Bærum and operates from bases at Stavanger Airport, Sola, and Haugesund Airport, Karmøy in Norway, and Rigil in the UK. Bristow Norway operates two types of helicopter; the Eurocopter AS332 L2 Super Puma and the Sikorsky S-92.
In October 2013, Bristow acquired the remaining 51% of Bristow Norway from HS. The company was renamed to Bristow Helicopters AS on 17 November 2013. The company was renamed to Bristow AS on 11 July 2016.

The Empire has also begun a program known as Project Harvester, where they harvest the Force from Force-sensitive children, and train them to be their future soldiers.

A group of Jedi loyalists, including the former Jedi Master Luke Skywalker, have established a resistance cell, which is attempting to gather children from across the galaxy to train them in the ways of the Force. Luke and his comrades are using a ship known as the Ghost to smuggle children across the galaxy. The Ghost and its crew are currently doing so with the help of the Twi'lek Hera Syndulla, her pilot brother Zeb, and the crew of their starship, the Raddus, led by Chopper. The Ghost's crew is made up of the rebels Kanan Jarrus, Ezra Bridger, Sabine Wren, and her friends.

The crew of the Ghost, however, is able to escape the Inquisitor's clutches.

The crew of the Ghost then travels to the planet of Dathomir, where they meet the Witches of Dathomir, who are in conflict with the Empire. They are also joined by the Padawan Ezra, who has been captured by the Inquisitor, and has been stuck in the Dark Side of the Force.

The prognosis for patients with APL is excellent if the disease is recognized early and treated appropriately. The high cure rate is largely due to the identification and use of a drug, all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA), that has no cytotoxic properties but has transforming activity on malignant promyelocytes, inducing them to differentiate into normal neutrophils. ATRA is the only drug that has cured patients with APL.
The goal of treatment is to induce complete remission as soon as possible, with the intention of eliminating the disease before it can cause damage to other organs. If complete remission can be achieved , then the prognosis of the patient is excellent.  After achieving remission, the patient can be treated with chemotherapy and given an opportunity to be cured.
ATRA is used in conjunction with chemotherapy to eliminate the leukemic cells that have not been differentiated by ATRA. This is a major distinction between APL and other forms of leukemia.
Other forms of leukemia have a higher rate of relapse. Relapse does not mean that the patient's disease is incurable; rather, it means that the patient, even after initial treatment, continues to have abnormal blood cells. However, because the treatment for APL is so effective, the need to treat relapse is reduced, and the prognosis for relapse is very good.
When it is necessary to treat relapse, the treatment that is used is a combination of an all-trans retinoic acid-based induction program and chemotherapy. The combination is successful in eliminating relapse, and the prognosis for relapse is good.

A topological ordering of a directed graph is an ordering of its vertices into a sequence , such that for every edge the start

vertex comes before the end vertex. Unlike a topological ordering of a tree, in which the ordering coincides with the natural order of the vertices, the ordering of a directed acyclic graph may vary from one vertex to another.

For example, the graph

```
       a

     b    c
    / \   \
   d    e   f
  / \     \
 g    h     j
```

has three possible topological orderings: a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h, j; b, c, d, e, f, g, h, j, a; a, c, d, e, f, g, h, j, b. A different topological ordering of this graph is the one in which the vertices are numbered in the natural order.

Thus, a topological ordering of a directed acyclic graph cannot be defined by giving a single ordering, but instead must be given as a set of possible orderings.

This is given by the topological sorting problem, which is NP-complete.

## Plot

The film begins with a young boy named Quasimodo, who lives in a church in Paris, France. The boy is deformed and is ridiculed by the townspeople, especially the local Archdeacon Frollo. When he is nine years old, Frollo takes Quasimodo to a traveling circus, where he is witness to a performance by the beautiful Esmeralda.

Twenty years later, Quasimodo is a bell-ringer in Notre Dame Cathedral. Frollo, now a priest, often visits him. He gives Quasimodo a book about the true identity of the gargoyles on Notre Dame.

One day, Frollo visits Quasimodo and tells him that he knows the identity of the gypsy woman Esmeralda. Quasimodo is angered and does not want to help Frollo, but Frollo forces him to go without revealing the fate of Esmeralda. Quasimodo and Frollo follow Esmeralda and a band of gypsies to the Festival of Fools and the Feast of Fools. As the festival begins, Quasimodo helps Esmeralda avoid the crowd.

Quasimodo and Esmeralda meet and fall in love. As she is about to leave, Frollo appears and abducts Esmeralda. Quasimodo follows Frollo to the house of Phoebus. Phoebus and his men beat Quasimodo, and Frollo reveals his plan to kill Esmeralda. Quasimodo escapes and rescues Esmeralda, who reveals that she is a prisoner of the house. Quasimodo and Esmeralda escape and hide in Notre Dame.

The next day, Quasimodo and Esmeralda are caught by Frollo. Phoebus discovers Quasimodo with Esmeralda and chases them. Quasimodo helps Esmeralda to escape, but is injured trying to do so. Esmeralda finds Frollo, who is trying to kill her, and reveals her pregnancy. Frollo is horrified that Esmeralda was not a virgin when she conceived. He begins to beat Esmeralda, but is stopped by Quasimodo. They are both caught by the guards.

Phoebus discovers that Quasimodo and Esmeralda escaped. He decides to help Quasimodo save her. They go to the cemetery where Esmeralda is being held. -@ play. Newell also said that Valve intends to support Dota 2 by "just having fun making it" and that Valve was "not going to be a publisher" for the game with regards to adding new content. In July 2013, Newell stated that Dota 2 was profitable, and Valve's business model for Dota 2 was to treat it as a service, not a product, and to make money from the sale of cosmetic items rather than selling the game itself.
 Valve released the Dota 2 client as a free download, running on the Source engine, in July 2011, with the release of the game's first publicly available custom map, "The Duel". The game was removed from Steam's list of available titles in late July 2011, with the release of the game's first custom game mode "The Arcade". A closed beta was held in the fall of 2011 for invite-only participants, and after the beta had concluded Valve announced that the game would enter "Open Beta" in April 2012. On April 3, 2012, Valve announced that the game had officially entered "Open Beta".
A beta period was held between March and May 2013, and a closed beta was held between April and June 2013. There was also a free-to-play weekend in March 2014, which allowed anyone to play the game for free.

Dota 2 is a multiplayer online battle arena (MOBA) game that takes elements from the Warcraft III custom map Defense of the Ancients (DotA) and modifies them to comply with the Source engine.
Dota 2 is a free-to-play game.
The basic format of the game is that two teams of five players each must battle to defend their base, the Ancient, as well as destroy the opposing team's Ancient. Players control one of 110 playable characters, known as 'heroes', each of which has a unique style of play. The game is played on a map that is divided into three lanes that stretch across the length of the map and are separated by a river. The lanes are connected by two "jungle" paths that are home to neutral creeps that respawn continuously. The main resources in Dota 2 are experience and gold, which are earned by killing creeps, neutrals and enemy heroes and are used for leveling up and purchasing items respectively. At the end of each match, players are ranked based on their MMR (Matchmaking Rating), which is determined by their match history and performance. These ranks are used to match players of similar skill in subsequent games.
The main objective of each team is to destroy the other team's Ancient. Each team begins the game with a single Ancient located in their respective base. To destroy the Ancient of the opposing team, players must pass through their own three lanes to reach the Ancient. Each lane has three levels that must be traversed to reach the lane's last tower, which is guarded by a powerful structure known as the Ancient. Each tower is defended by a group of defensive structures called creeps, which respawn continuously.
Dota 2 features many game modes, including the main "All Pick" mode, which allows players to pick any hero they desire. Other game modes include "Captain's Draft", "Roles", "Arena", and "Solo-Mid". In "Captain's Draft", the team's captain picks a hero for each player on the team. In "Roles", the captain picks a role for each player on the team to match their play style. In "Arena", the players start with the same heroes and items as they do in All Pick mode. In "Solo-Mid", players are only allowed to pick heroes that can be played solo.
Dota 2 features an item-based progression system in which players can purchase stronger and more numerous items for their heroes to improve their stats, abilities, and effects. The game features over 200 different items that are divided into 12 different categories, each with its own unique function and effect. Each item has a level requirement that must be met before it can be used by a hero. Once an item is purchased, it is permanently attached to the hero and cannot be removed from them.

The first named storm formed out of the interaction between tropical wave and a mid @-@ level tropospheric trough northeast of

97°W as the upper-level environment was favorable for tropical cyclone development. A mid-tropospheric trough was moving eastward into the region and an upper-level low was located to the west of the wave. This allowed for the wave to interact with the trough and produce a surface low. The first named storm was officially declared on September 10, 2008, at 2100 UTC when the center of Tropical Storm Liza was located at 15.0°N, 80.3°W. Liza was the first named storm to form in the Atlantic basin in the month of September since the 2008 Atlantic hurricane season began on June 1. Liza was also the earliest named storm on record in the Atlantic basin to form in the month of September.
Liza subsequently intensified into a Category 1 hurricane on September 11, 2008, at 0600 UTC, when its maximum sustained winds reached 185 km/h (115 mph). Liza was the earliest Category 1 hurricane on record to form in the Atlantic basin in the month of September. The hurricane continued to intensify as it moved westward and intensified into a Category 2 hurricane on September 12, 2008, at 0600 UTC, when the peak winds reached 220 km/h (140 mph). Liza continued to intensify and reached its peak intensity as a Category 3 hurricane with maximum sustained winds of 240 km/h (150 mph) at 0600 UTC on September 13, 2008.
Liza began to weaken as it moved westward and into an area with strong shear. Liza was downgraded to a Category 2 hurricane on September 14, 2008, at 1500 UTC, when its peak winds reached 195 km/h (120 mph). The hurricane continued to weaken as it moved into cooler waters and was downgraded to a Category 1 hurricane on September 15, 2008, at 0600 UTC, when its peak winds reached 185 km/h (115 mph). Liza was subsequently downgraded to a Category 1 hurricane on September 16, 2008, at 0600 UTC, when its peak winds reached 175 km/h (110 mph). The hurricane continued to weaken and was downgraded to a tropical storm on September 17, 2008, at 0600 UTC, when its peak winds reached 110 km/h (70 mph). Liza was subsequently downgraded to a tropical storm on September 18, 2008, at 0600 UTC, when its peak winds reached 95 km/h (60 mph). The storm was subsequently downgraded to a tropical depression on September 19, 2008, at 0600 UTC, when the peak winds reached 65 km/h (40 mph). At 1500 UTC on September 20, 2008, the NHC reported that Liza had become extratropical as it began to interact with a mid-latitude frontal system.

Lesser Slave Lake is the largest lake in the province of Alberta and is located in the heart of Canada's prairie province. It is 720 km (448 mi) east of the Pacific Ocean and 120 km (75 mi) north of the US border. The lake is part of the Slave River watershed and is connected to the Arctic Ocean by the Slave River. Lesser Slave Lake is 110 km (68 mi) long, 8.5 km (5.3 mi) wide, and has a maximum depth of 34.5 m (113 ft). Lesser Slave Lake is a popular recreational destination with a variety of outdoor activities including fishing, canoeing, kayaking, camping, and wildlife viewing. The Importance of Being Earnest , A Trivial Comedy for Serious People is a play by Oscar Wilde . First performed on 14 February

1895 at the St James's Theatre in London, it is a farcical comedy in which the protagonists maintain fictitious personae to escape burdensome social obligations.
In The Importance of Being Earnest, Wilde satirizes the Victorian notion of a serious young man and creates four characters who live a lifestyle of trivial pursuits. The play's major theme is the triviality with which it treats institutions as serious as marriage.
The play's opening is among Wilde's most famous, and is often quoted : "We live in an age when unnecessary things are our only necessities."
The Importance of Being Earnest is one of the most performed comedies. It is the fourth most frequently performed work in English after Shakespeare 's Hamlet , A Midsummer Night's Dream and The Tempest , and is performed more often than either of the other two most-performed plays, George Bernard Shaw 's Pygmalion and Noël Coward 's Private Lives .
In 1894, Wilde lived at 16 Tite Street in Chelsea , west London, with his mother, Jane, and two young children, Cyril and Vyvyan. A frequent visitor to Wilde's home was his former Oxford contemporary, Robert Sherard, and Wilde had also recently renewed contact with another friend, Charles Haigh-Adams .
Sherard and Haigh-Adams were both authors. Wilde had been impressed by Sherard's book of poetry, The Wind Before the Storm , and the two men became good friends. Sherard introduced Wilde to the actress Lillie Langtry .
Wilde was also re-establishing contact with his former lover, Lord Alfred Douglas, who was one of the sons of the Marquess of Queensberry . He was also beginning to see Douglas' mother, the Marchioness of Queensberry, more frequently.
The Marquess of Queensberry was a notoriously difficult man, a former boxer who had been famous for his skill during the 1850s and '60s. He had also been a major patron of the arts, including theatre.
The play's main characters, Algernon Moncrieff and Jack Worthing, are both in earnest pursuit of their love interests, Cecily Cardew and Gwendolen Fairfax, who are both daughters of a fictitious half-batty old gentleman called Bunbury .
The play is a satire on the Victorian obsession with social prestige, and explores the importance of being earnest .
Wilde's first play, Vera , was performed privately in 1884 at the home of his friend Henry Arthur Jones . Wilde's second play, Lady Windermere's Fan , was produced in London in 1892 and was a great success. His next play, A Woman of No Importance , was also successful.
On 18 February 1891, Wilde's only child, Cyril, was born to his mistress, the actress Lillie Langtry . Wilde had taken Langtry to Paris to be his mistress, and she had returned to England with the child. Wilde was refused custody of his son, and Langtry was given custody.
In 1893, Wilde wrote The Ideal Husband , which was not a success. He then travelled to the United States, where he met American businessman and playwright Charles Frohman . Frohman had been impressed by Wilde's earlier work, and he suggested that Wilde write a play for him. Wilde agreed to write a play for Frohman, in return for which Frohman would finance a tour of America.
The play that Frohman wanted Wilde to write was called The Importance of Being Earnest . Frohman asked Wilde to name his own price for the play. Wilde demanded $1,000, and Frohman agreed to pay this amount to Wilde.
Frohman then asked Wilde to write a play for him to be performed in London. Wilde agreed to write a play called A Woman of No Importance .
On 20 February 1895, The Importance of Being Earnest was first performed at the St James's Theatre. It was a success, and was followed by another successful run at the Haymarket Theatre.
The play was then taken to the United States, where it opened at the Lyceum Theatre in New York City on 14 March 1895. The play was well received, and ran for 10 days.

He was born at Greenock, Renfrewshire, Scotland, the son of James Torrens (1758–1821), a merchant, of Liverpool, and his wife, Isabella, daughter of the Rev. He was educated at the High School, Glasgow, at Edinburgh Academy, and at the University of Edinburgh. After qualifying as a doctor, he was in practice in Liverpool until 1841, when he removed to London. In 1831 he married, at Liverpool, Miss Jane Tanner, daughter of James Tanner, of Liverpool, and had by her six children: two sons, James (1832–1918) and Charles (1836–1864), who were both educated at Trinity Hall, Cambridge, and died unmarried; and four daughters, who married respectively Sir Francis Maclean, bart., of Raasay, Duncan McPherson of Greenock, Alexander Fletcher of Glasgow, and John McKenzie of Dundee.
Torrens died at his residence in Chelsea, London, on 20 July 1867.

As of 2003 there were still 138 Allied men with no known grave in the area , and they are commemorated at the Groesbeek Memoria

al. Among them are 11 Canadians and two Americans who were buried on the spot where they fell, and the remaining 127 were buried in two temporary cemeteries which were then destroyed. In 1946 the Groesbeek Canadian Cemetery was established and the remains of the buried men were transferred there. The two US soldiers are buried in the US Military Cemetery in Margraten. The names of all these men are on the Wall of Remembrance in Groesbeek.
The memorial is a 150 metre long wall, 5 metres high, divided in 11 sections of 13 metres. Each section contains the names of 60 men who died in the Groesbeek area during the liberation of the Netherlands.
The memorial was designed by the Dutch architect J.C. Theunissen, who was assisted by Dutch artist H. Kuiper. The unveiling took place on 24 May 2000, exactly 56 years after the liberation of Groesbeek by the Canadian 3rd Infantry Division. In the presence of the Queen of the Netherlands, Princess Margriet, the names of those 138 men were read, and flowers were laid under the memorial.
The idea for the memorial came from the American city of Norfolk, Virginia, which has a similar memorial for the American soldiers who have fallen in the liberation of the Netherlands. The American Memorial in Norfolk was unveiled in 1999. The Dutch memorial in Groesbeek was the first memorial for the liberation of the Netherlands to be erected in the country.
The memorial was funded by the Canadian government, the Dutch government and the families of the 138 men.

Ahead of their first campaign in Division One , Bradford City embarked upon their first continental tour ; despite victories ov

er Montpellier and Marseille, three draws in a series of friendlies with Feyenoord , Sporting Lisbon and Athletic Bilbao made the tour something of a disappointment. As a result of the second game against Athletic Bilbao, Ken Furphy , the City manager, made an unscheduled trip to the Basque country and took a flight to Vitoria. He was travelling alone and was forced to make his own way to the next port of call in Lisbon, where he was visited by the City chairman, Jack Tordoff, and vice-chairman, Jack Hill . 'I'm here simply to bring you the good news,' said Hill , 'that you're staying at Bradford City.'
Hill was referring to the fact that Tordoff had finally succumbed to pressure and withdrawn his offer to purchase the club. Furphy had been assured that the chairman would not sell the club and was not particularly disturbed when he learned that this was not the case. He had been offered a severance package which included a £1,000 bonus, a year's wages and a car. He duly accepted and the following day a statement was released confirming the cessation of negotiations.
The City management and board had been aware of the chairman's intentions since May , when Tordoff issued a statement confirming his belief that the club was on the verge of bankruptcy. From this point on, the chairman attempted to sell the club to a number of interested parties, including an agent representing two Arab sheikhs, a consortium of Indian businessmen and a group of investors from Hong Kong. In the summer of 1982, he approached a local property developer, Harold Rhodes , who was prepared to take a long-term view and, in return for a guarantee of funds, offered to make a significant contribution to the club's wage bill. Rhodes had already provided £150,000 to cover the season's admission prices, but his offer was rejected and, shortly afterwards, he was forced to sell his interest in the club to a group of local businessmen.
Tordoff's attempt to sell the club had caused friction in the boardroom and the chairman was forced to resign his place on the board. This left the club in a unique position, where the chairman was no longer involved in running the club. Both Furphy and assistant manager, Bobby Saxton , were left in a position of power.
The City management had become concerned with the chairman's behaviour and had contacted the Professional Footballers Association. The PFA, in turn, had contacted the Football Association, who referred the matter to the police. However, as the chairman's behaviour was deemed to be harassment rather than an assault, the police were unable to take any action. Moreover, because of the impending court case, the PFA decided to withdraw their support and, as a result, the chairman was able to continue his activities.
In September, the chairman was accused by the club's accountant, David Massey , of threatening to make a complaint to the police. Tordoff was later charged with making a false statement to the police and was fined £300. The club had been under investigation for some months and, in late 1985, the police began to monitor the chairman 's activities, which included frequent visits to the City of Bradford Football Club offices.
In April 1986, Tordoff was convicted of criminal damage and given a five-year conditional discharge. The police subsequently dropped their investigation into his behaviour.
The chairman was forced to withdraw his offer to purchase the club in May and the following month he was fined £200,000 by the High Court. Tordoff was ordered to pay a further £300,000 in damages to the club. The court also warned Tordoff that he would not be allowed to hold a position of influence within the club.
The chairman's behaviour had caused considerable problems for the club and the City management were forced to work on a shoestring budget. In 1988, the club was placed in administration and, in 1989, the club was taken over by a consortium of local businessmen.
The chairman's actions had significantly damaged the club's reputation, with the chairman's behaviour being widely reported. In the years that followed, the club was subject to a number of unsuccessful takeover bids and, subsequently, the club was taken over by a consortium of local businessmen.

Some of the top river rafting destinations in Montana include Beaverhead River, Clark Fork River, Canyon Ferry Lake, Gallatin River, Lower Clark Fork River, Lochsa River, Lower Madison River, Missouri River, Rock Creek, and Yellowstone River.

The Beaverhead River is a popular river rafting destination for its scenic beauty and whitewater.

The text editing environment in Emacs uses a double space following a period to identify the end of sentences unambiguously ; t

here are many ways to do this, but the most important thing to realize is that once you decide how to do it you need to do it consistently.  If you let your editing habits wander from one unambiguous way to another  you will eventually have to fix the formatting somewhere or other.  You might as well fix it all at once  and stay consistent.
 If you are using the Emacs standalone package, you can use the command M-x set-mark-command to change how the cursor moves when you press the space-bar to move the cursor to the end of sentences.  For example, the command M-x set-mark-command 'move-to-paragraph-end (or move-to-paragraph-end-command) moves the cursor to the end of the paragraph.  You might as well use this command to move the cursor to the end of sentences as well.  To do this, issue the command M-x set-mark-command "move-to-paragraph-and-end-of-sentence" and the command M-x set-mark-command 'move-to-paragraph-and-end-of-sentence will move the cursor to the end of the sentence and the paragraph.
 This command is not part of the Emacs package.  You can include it in your Emacs configuration file using the command M-x customize-group 'set-mark-command to add it to the menu of commands available at M-x set-mark-command.  To enable this command in the standalone package, put the command M-x set-mark-command 'move-to-paragraph-and-end-of-sentence in the file emacs/lisp/init.el.

The Battle of Alam Halfa Ridge was a major battle of the Second World War fought during the Second Battle of El Alamein. The battle was fought in late August 1942, when the Eighth Army under Lieutenant-General Bernard Montgomery attacked the Axis forces of the Panzer Army Africa under Field Marshal Erwin Rommel in the Alam Halfa Ridge area, 30 km (19 mi) west of the coastal town of El Alamein. The British attack was preceded by a four-day artillery bombardment delivered by the Royal Artillery and other Commonwealth forces. The bombardment was intended to destroy German defences, but the Germans' anti-tank ditches and wire obstacles survived the bombardment. The British attackers advanced through minefields and anti-tank ditches into strong defensive positions, where they used smoke to cover their advance and attempted to bypass many strongpoints. The battle was costly for both sides, with British and Indian casualties of 2,150 men killed, 6,787 men wounded and 158 missing; the Germans and Italians suffered 1,500 killed, 3,000 wounded and 3,000 missing. The battle is considered one of Montgomery's finest achievements, and he had conceived the battle plan in just five days.
The Battle of Alam Halfa Ridge took place as part of the Second Battle of El Alamein, which was the second of three major battles fought between the Eighth Army and Panzer Army Africa, after the First Battle of El Alamein. The Eighth Army, under Lieutenant-General Bernard Montgomery, was attempting to destroy the Afrika Korps under Field Marshal Erwin Rommel, and the Panzer Army's morale and fighting ability. The Eighth Army had been defeated in the First Battle of El Alamein, and Montgomery had been relieved of his command, due to his perceived lack of aggression. After a reorganisation of the Eighth Army, and a lengthy period in which the armour and artillery were refitted, Montgomery began to plan his next offensive. The Battle of Alam Halfa Ridge was the first stage of Montgomery's Alamein Line operations.
The Alam Halfa Ridge was a series of plateaux 30 kilometres (19 mi) west of El Alamein in Egypt. The ridge formed the easternmost edge of the British defensive perimeter, extending south from the Qattara Depression in the west to the coastal region at El Daba. On the ridge, the Axis forces had created a defensive line, with a series of strongpoints, that had been built up over time. The Germans and Italians had not been expecting an attack in this area, and the defences were not strong enough to withstand the expected attack.
The Second Battle of El Alamein was fought during the Western Desert Campaign of the Second World War, near El Alamein in the Mediterranean theatre. The battle comprised two major British offensives that took place in July and August 1942, and was followed by a short period of static front-line fighting. The battles were fought in the western part of the Egyptian desert between the Mediterranean coast, west of El Alamein, and Qattara Depression, south of the Qattara Depression.

The 1990 eastern North Pacific hurricane season was active in terms of number of storms that attained at least tropical storm intensity. There were a total of 23 tropical depressions, 15 tropical storms, and three hurricanes in the basin. This was the third consecutive season to have at least three hurricanes, and only the fourth time in history that three hurricanes formed in a single season. However, the season was below-average in terms of the accumulated cyclone energy (ACE) index, which was 12% below the long-term average.
The season officially began on May 15, 1990, and ended on November 30. These dates conventionally delimit the periods of each year when most tropical cyclones form in the eastern North Pacific basin. The hurricane season's first tropical cyclone, Tropical Depression One-E, formed on June 27, making this season the first since 1962 to have no named storms prior to the season's official start date.
This season was also notable for the formation of Hurricane Eugene, which was retrospectively classified as a Category 4 hurricane. The first tropical cyclone to form in the eastern Pacific, Eugene was one of only three Category 4 hurricanes of the season, and the only to form prior to the official start of the season.
The first and only tropical depression of the season, Tropical Depression One-E, formed on June 27. On July 1, the system strengthened into Tropical Storm Gladys as it passed about 200 mi (320 km) south of Cabo San Lucas. The storm strengthened further and became a hurricane later that day. On July 3, Gladys passed about 200 mi (320 km) southwest of Cabo San Lucas, and the system weakened back into a tropical storm. By early on July 4, Gladys weakened into a tropical depression. The next day, Gladys dissipated near the Baja California Peninsula. The remnants of Gladys later moved onto the Gulf of California on July 6.
Hurricane Gerry was the second tropical cyclone of the season and the third named storm. The system formed on July 6, about 800 mi (1,300 km) southwest of Manzanillo, Mexico. At the time, Gerry was considered to be a Category 1 hurricane. On July 8, Gerry reached its peak strength as a Category 2 hurricane with maximum sustained winds of 105 mph (165 km/h) and a minimum barometric pressure of 970 mbar (28.6 inHg). After Gerry passed near Acapulco, the cyclone weakened and dissipated on July 12.
Hurricane Hortense was the third storm of the season and the second system to reach Category 3 status. Hortense was declared to be a tropical storm on July 15 and a hurricane on July 16. By July 17, Hortense was upgraded to a Category 3 hurricane with maximum sustained winds of 120 mph (195 km/h) and a minimum barometric pressure of 965 mbar (28.5 inHg). The hurricane later reached its peak strength as a Category 4 hurricane with maximum sustained winds of 130 mph (210 km/h) and a minimum barometric pressure of 960 mbar (28.3 inHg). Hortense weakened slightly before making landfall near Salina Cruz, Mexico. After moving inland, Hortense gradually weakened and dissipated on July 19.
Hurricane Ingrid was the fourth named storm of the season. Ingrid formed on July 22 out of a tropical wave that moved off the coast of Africa on July 18. Hurricane Ingrid was downgraded to a tropical storm on July 22 and a tropical depression on July 23. After Ingrid weakened, the cyclone moved inland and dissipated on July 25.
Hurricane Juliette was the fifth named storm and the second Category 3 hurricane of the season. Juliette was the first tropical cyclone of the season to form in the eastern Pacific, and the first to form prior to the official start of the season. The DuMont Television Network ( also known as the DuMont Network , simply DuMont / Du Mont , or ( incorrectly ) Dumont / duːmɒn

/ ) was one of the world 's pioneer commercial television networks, rivalling CBS , NBC , and ABC . The network was named after its founder, DuMont Laboratories founder Allen B. Drexel DuMont , who also founded the DuMont Television Network. Founded in 1944, the network was the first to operate on the west coast of the United States ( although its flagship station was based in New York City ).
The network was purchased by Paramount Pictures in 1956, and converted into a syndication service in 1957. Although DuMont was the first commercial television network in the United States, it was the smallest of the Big Three networks, and was unable to compete with its major rivals in terms of programming, ratings, and revenue.
The DuMont Television Network was founded in 1944 in Pittsburgh , Pennsylvania by Allen B. DuMont , who had purchased DuMont Laboratories in 1931. DuMont expanded the company into the manufacture of television apparatus, and by 1941 he had built a complete TV system.
He began broadcasting experimental television programs in 1942, and in February 1944, WABD (channel 5 ) in New York City began independent operation. The network soon began operations in other cities, including Philadelphia , Pittsburgh , and Los Angeles .
DuMont's network broadcasts were initially transmitted on NTSC , but as the FCC allowed independent stations to broadcast in color, DuMont adopted the format by the end of 1950. The network also used the NTSC 525-line standard until 1963, when it switched to color RCA's 800-line system.
DuMont's broadcasts were transmitted from a studio in the Empire State Building in New York City, and by around 1950, the network's vision and sound were converted to color. The network's original logo was a stylized red dot. Later, the logo was changed to a large stylized capital "D" in a blue circle.
By the early 1950s, DuMont had become the third largest of the Big Three television networks. The network's first President was C. H. McTavish (who was also President of DuMont Laboratories), and who was succeeded by Hildred Scott Form in 1951.
On July 12, 1951, DuMont made history when the network became the first to broadcast a coast-to-coast television broadcast, airing the U.S. Army-Air Force All-American Marching Band in New York City and transmitting it live to Los Angeles .
The early 1950s were the network's most successful years, with DuMont programming winning a primetime Emmy in 1951, and a total of four in 1952 and 1953. The network's most successful programs were the music and variety show Cavalcade of America , the children's series Uncle Milty, and the anthology series Climax! . Also in 1952, DuMont became the first network to broadcast coast-to-coast color television, with a broadcast of the Rose Bowl parade from Pasadena, California .
In the fall of 1952, the network's affiliate lineup was expanded to 10 stations, including WPTZ in Philadelphia , WPTC in Trenton , New Jersey , and WABD in New York City.
In the fall of 1953, DuMont launched a television production and syndication company called DuMont Television Productions , with the network's general manager John Donnelly serving as its president. In 1954, DuMont Television Productions began producing syndicated programs, including The Jackie Gleason Show and The Alan Young Show .
In 1955, DuMont formed a programming alliance with ABC , called the Television Arts and Sciences Association ( TASA ). The two networks agreed to produce two programs a week together, with DuMont programs airing on ABC (and vice versa). The alliance was formed to counter the dominance of CBS and NBC , and the two networks programmed against CBS's Ed Sullivan Show and NBC's Tonight Show .

The first recorded observation of the starry sky was by the Ancient Egyptians, who recognized that the Sun, the Moon, and the brightest planets could be used as a means of navigation and timekeeping. They used the second brightest star, Sirius, to measure the annual flooding of the Nile, and the planet Venus for religious observances. The Babylonians, whose civilization extended across the Middle East, were the first to record the positions of the stars in a systematic way (c. 3500 BC). They also made detailed maps of the Moon and developed a heliocentric system of planetary motions.
The Chinese were the first to identify the stars as distant suns and the first to record their proper motions across the sky, which were discovered by the Han Dynasty astronomer Hipparchus in the 2nd century BC. Chinese astronomy and mathematics (astronomy, calendar, mathematics, geography) was significantly further developed in the Han Dynasty (202 BC – 220 AD), during which the Chinese discovered the "sidereal year" and the length of the tropical year.
The earliest known star catalogues were created by the Babylonians , the Greeks and by the Indian astronomers. dates on the 2011 leg of the U2 360° Tour . It was the last song of the main set, and The Edge was accompanied onstage by a violinist and a cellist.  The song was also included during each show of the 2015 Innocence + Experience Tour . 

## Live performances

The live debut of the new arrangement was performed at the third night of U2 360° at the Rose Bowl, on June 22, 2009. The Edge had been considering the idea of playing the song solo in a similar manner to the band's performance of " Two Shots of Happy, One Shot of Sad " on the 1997–1998 PopMart Tour. He had played the song solo on the band's 2005–2006 Vertigo Tour, but had been playing the song with the rest of the band on the 2009–2011 leg of the U2 360° Tour . 

The song was first performed in Europe during the U2 360° Tour . The Edge performed the song solo at the second night of the band's second show in Gelsenkirchen, Germany on July 29, 2009.  The Edge has continued to play "Sunday Bloody Sunday" on solo during each show of the 2015 Innocence + Experience Tour .

Paranthodon was a small stegosaurid relative to larger relatives such as Stegosaurus . Thomas R. Holtz Jr. estimated that the a

pex predator of the Paranthodon's environment was the Carcharodontosauridae Tyrannotitan and that the environment was semi-arid.

## Significance

Paranthodon is important because it is one of the few known herbivorous stegosaurs. However, its tooth structure is very different from other stegosaurs and it is not clear if it should be included in Stegosauria. Additionally, Paranthodon's teeth appear to be more like those of herbivorous ornithopods than those of other stegosaurs, suggesting that Paranthodon was most closely related to ornithopod groups rather than stegosaurs.

## Phylogeny

Paranthodon was named in 1979 by Sven Sachs and William J.K. Hutchison. It is known from teeth. Paranthodon was originally thought to be a stegosaur. However, it is now regarded as a basal ornithopod.
" West End Girls " has been generally well received by music critics . Stephen Thomas Erlewine from Allmusic in a review of the

album described the song as a "wistful electric piano ballad with a haunting melody and subtle harmonies"  and a "soulful ballad". 

In 1999, " West End Girls " was ranked No. 248 on Rolling Stone's list of the 500 Greatest Songs of All Time .  In 1999, NME ranked the song No. 19 on its list of "The Top 150 Singles of the Past 15 Years".

### Japan

"West End Girls" was a Top 20 hit in Japan, where it was released in 1985 as a single from the album The Very Best of Pet Shop Boys. It also appeared on the Best of Pet Shop Boys 2 compilation.

### Other countries

The song was a top 20 hit in Australia and New Zealand.

In 1868 , Proctor was built as a company town in the midst of the timber required for the tannery ( Barbours had initially been

tanners).

The town was incorporated in 1895.
Barboursville Tannery continued to be a major employer in Proctor until the early 1930s, when the business was purchased by the Troxell Leather Company.

The historic Barboursville Tannery, along with the surrounding Proctor village, was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1989.

According to the United States Census Bureau, the CDP has a total area of 3.7 square miles (9.6 km²), of which 3.7 square miles (9.6 km²) is land and 0.04 square miles (0.10 km²) (0.82%) is water.

## Demographics

As of the census of 2000, there were 1,379 people, 606 households, and 364 families residing in the CDP. The population density was 370.4 people per square mile (143.0/km²). There were 665 housing units at an average density of 175.6/sq mi (67.8/km²). The racial makeup of the CDP was 97.74% White, 0.37% African American, 0.22% Native American, 0.37% Asian, 0.29% Pacific Islander, 0.15% from other races, and 0.74% from two or more races. Hispanic or Latino of any race were 0.94% of the population.

There were 606 households, out of which 23.8% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 46.0% were married couples living together, 8.4% had a female householder with no husband present, and 42.8% were non-families. 37.2% of all households were made up of individuals, and 17.0% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.11 and the average family size was 2.78.

In the CDP, the population was spread out, with 19.2% under the age of 18, 5.5% from 18 to 24, 22.9% from 25 to 44, 22.8% from 45 to 64, and 29.6% who were 65 years of age or older. The median age was 45 years. For every 100 females, there were 86.0 males. For every 100 females age 18 and over, there were 79.4 males.

The median income for a household in the CDP was $26,990, and the median income for a family was $35,573. Males had a median income of $25,227 versus $18,824 for females. The per capita income for the CDP was $15,214. About 5.9% of families and 13.4% of the population were below the poverty line, including 27.5% of those under age 18 and 17.7% of those age 65 or over.

I think a strong case can be made that political assassination actually does change things . If you look at the assassinations

in the 1960s, you can see that it changed the course of the history of the United States. That's a hard thing to argue.
—LARRY BUCHANAN,  
head of the U.S. Secret Service
The assassination of President John F. Kennedy changed the course of history. The murder of Martin Luther King Jr. was a catalyst for a social revolution in the United States. The killing of Malcolm X accelerated racial tensions in the nation. And the assassination of Robert Kennedy was a symbol of the violence in American society at the time.
A close look at these and other assassinations in recent years suggests that they may have had an even greater impact on the lives of the people responsible for carrying them out.
In the United States, an estimated 10,000 people are serving life sentences for crimes they didn't commit, according to the Innocence Project, a nonprofit legal organization that works to exonerate wrongly convicted prisoners. The organization cites as one of the main reasons for these wrongful convictions the fact that witnesses "often deliberately lie to the police, prosecutors or judges."
Another reason is that the memory of the assassinations of the 1960s have led to the appointment of prosecutors who are determined to put people in jail for their crimes.
The result is a system that is heavily skewed against the accused.
"We have a system that has a built-in bias," said Barry Scheck, one of the co-founders of the Innocence Project and a lawyer for the group. "And it's a bias that says, 'I'm going to get the conviction, and I'm not going to look at the evidence.' "
The result, says John Grisham, author of _The Innocent Man,_ is that "the system is broken."
"It's broken in a lot of ways, but the one that has to be fixed is the way witnesses are treated," Grisham says. "The system has to be fixed so that we can convict people who are guilty, but we can't convict people who are innocent."
The Innocence Project has a number of cases that are proof that the system has failed.
"The first thing the police do is they talk to witnesses," Scheck said. "And that's very dangerous. It's like a fishing expedition. They're looking for a match, and they're willing to take false testimony."
Scheck said that in some cases, the police have used the testimony of a witness who was later proven to be lying to "build a case" against an innocent person.
"In some cases, the police are willing to take false testimony from a witness and use it to build a case against an innocent person," Scheck said. "They're willing to go to extremes to get a conviction.
"It's a system that's broken in a lot of ways," he said. "But the one that has to be fixed is the way witnesses are treated."
In 2010, the Innocence Project took on the case of Curtis Flowers, who was convicted of killing four people in a Mississippi grocery store. The case was unusual in that Flowers was convicted in the same trial as his brother, who was not charged.
"The brother was on trial for a different crime," Scheck said. "But the brother was still charged with the same crime. So there was a two-pronged attack."
Flowers was convicted of the murders, and he was sentenced to death. But on appeal, the case was reversed, and Flowers was released from prison.
The case was the first time that the Innocence Project had successfully overturned a death sentence.
"This case should be an eye-opener to everybody about how the system is broken," Scheck said. "There are so many cases where the system is broken, and this is one of the most egregious cases that we've seen."
Flowers' life sentence was reversed, but he was still imprisoned for the rest of his life.
"It's an outrage," Scheck said. "You have a man who is innocent and he's in prison for the rest of his life. And it's a system that's broken in a lot of ways, but the one that has to be fixed is the way witnesses are treated."
