The Patriarchal Cathedral of the Holy Ascension of God ( Bulgarian : Патриаршеска катедрала „ Свето Възнесение Господне “ , Pat

rıaršeska katedrala „ Sveto Văznese Gospodne “ ) is a Bulgarian Orthodox cathedral in the capital Sofia. The cathedral is the seat of the Bulgarian Patriarch and the Patriarchal Synod of the Bulgarian Orthodox Church . The cathedral was built in 1904-1907 by the famous Bulgarian architectural designer Kolyo Ficheto and is considered to be one of the most beautiful examples of the Bulgarian Neo-Byzantine style .
The exterior of the cathedral is decorated with a mixture of various architectural elements from the different periods of the Bulgarian church history: columns from the churches of the 10th century – Champagne Palace of Preslav , Sveta Petka Church in Veliko Tarnovo , the central door from the church in Sveshtari , the capitals of the 12th-13th centuries – medieval churches in Turnovo , the second half of the 14th century – the church in Melnik , the 16th century – the church in Rila .
The decoration of the cathedral is a unique synthesis of the ornaments of the different periods of the Bulgarian culture, inspired by national folklore, and the architectural design of the cathedral is a synthesis of the Byzantine and Bulgarian national school. The interior of the church includes icons, frescoes and mosaics.
The cathedral is built on an area of ​​1 337 square meters. It is built in the form of a cross with three naves and a dome. The facade of the cathedral is 57 meters high. The interior of the building is 41 meters high, 43 meters wide and 11 meters deep. The church has 11 chapels, two altars and a baptistery. The cathedral is built of white stone .
The cathedral was consecrated on May 25 (May 12, old calendar) 1907 by the Bulgarian Patriarch Iriney with the help of Bulgarian Patriarchs Alexander, Kiril, Peter II, and other hierarchs and clergy. In 1995, the cathedral was reconstructed and renovated. It is the largest and most important cathedral in Bulgaria.
The cathedral was built in the period of the Bulgarian National Revival and, as such, it represents one of the most important achievements of Bulgarian architecture and art of the late 19th century, alongside the Zograf Monastery and the Church of the Ascension in the village of Rila .

@-@ Fleas are a serious problem in poultry , both in terms of health and welfare , and are a major source of income loss .
 @-@ What environment is the hen flea found in ?
@-@ The hen flea is a parasite of birds , although it is not exclusively so .
@-@ The species is cosmopolitan and is found wherever there are birds .
@-@ Hens and other domestic fowl are the main hosts found in the UK .
@-@ Wild bird species such as pheasants , partridges and pigeons have been used in surveys to determine the distribution of the hen flea .
@-@ The hen flea can be found on many other species of wild birds .
 @-@ How does the hen flea survive ?
@-@ The hen flea has a complex life cycle involving the egg , larva , pupa and adult stages .
@-@ The eggs are laid on the host's feathers and hatch in 3 to 14 days depending on temperature .
@-@ The larvae develop on the feathers and feed on feather debris .
@-@ The larvae pupate in the feather or in the soil and the adult fleas emerge several weeks later .
@-@ The adult fleas feed on the host and can live up to 12 months .
@-@ The life cycle can be completed within 2-3 months in summer and may take up to 12 months in winter .
 @-@ Fleas are very small and can be difficult to see without a magnifying glass .
@-@ The hen flea is about 1.7-2.5 mm long .
@-@ The colour varies from light brown to black and the legs are brown .
@-@ The adult fleas are usually darker than the larvae and pupae .
@-@ The eggs are tiny and are often only seen when they are found attached to the host's feathers .
@-@ The larvae are about 2 mm long and are whitish with brown legs .
@-@ The pupae are about 1 mm long .
@-@ The adult female fleas are larger than the males .
@-@ The male fleas are smaller than the females and are usually black or dark brown .

@-@ Fleas can infest homes by crawling indoors from the nesting site of infested birds .

Norman Campbell was a magician and illusionist who was born in 1920 in Stirling.
He started off performing in the family's variety club in Stirling, which had been opened by his father, Bill Campbell.
Norman's father had a variety club in Partick, and Norman's mother was a singer.
Norman's big break came when he was asked to perform in the South of England by the Mills Brothers.
He was only nineteen years old when he performed for the first time in London.
His stage name, 'The Great Cherry', was given to him by Jimmy James, who thought that it sounded more 'glamorous'.
Norman's act was based on mentalism and mind-reading, and he performed a trick called 'The Cat and the Hat'.
The idea behind the trick was that he would show the audience an empty hat and a small cat, and then ask them to imagine a white hat.
He would then ask the audience to put the hat back in the box, and would then perform a series of other tricks to show that the audience had successfully imagined the white hat.
Norman's main claim to fame was being the first person to perform the double-lift card trick on television, and he was the first magician to perform for both the Queen and the Pope.
He also wrote a book called _The Great Cherry, How to do Sleight of Hand_ , which was one of the first books to be written about magic and sleight of hand.
He also appeared in the 1964 film _The Magic Christian_ , starring Peter Sellers and Orson Welles.

 The Chapel of Our Lady of Sorrows ( Spanish : Capilla de Nuestra Señora de los Dolores ) , formerly known as the Chapel of the 17 Holy Helpers ( Capilla de los 17 Heladores ) , is a Roman Catholic chapel located in the former Convent of Our Lady of Sorrows ( Hospedería de Nuestra Señora de los Dolores ) , in the historic center of Mexico City . Tax ID :

## History

The main façade of the Chapel of Our Lady of Sorrows, designed by Manuel Tolsá

The convent was founded in 1608 by Spanish Franciscan friars and dedicated to Our Lady of Sorrows. The chapel was built during the 17th century. It was built by Manuel Tolsá , who designed the main façade of the chapel, the original bell tower and the interior windows.

The interior of the chapel is composed of a single nave. The main altarpiece of the chapel was designed by the Spanish artist Francisco Antonio de Lorenzana , who was the official painter and sculptor of the Franciscan Order in Mexico. The altarpiece was executed by Lorenzana and the carver Juan José de Labastida . The altarpiece is located on the main altar, which is flanked by two side altars.

Prior to 1816, the chapel was one of the main meeting places of the independence movement, especially during the government of the Spanish viceroy Marquess of the Valle de Oaxaca. On November 28, 1816, after a meeting, the independence movement marched on the Palacio Nacional .

The convent was closed in 1865 by the government of Benito Juárez , the Franciscans were exiled and the convent was converted into a school. Since the 19th century, the convent has been used as a public library. During the 20th century, the convent was used to house the National Museum of Anthropology, until the museum was transferred to its current location.

In 1930, the chapel was restored with the help of the Mexican painter and muralist David Alfaro Siqueiros , who painted several murals depicting scenes from the life of Christ. In 1994, the chapel was restored again, this time to its original design of Manuel Tolsá .

The game was designed to appeal to a broader audience than previous music video game titles, and includes support for up to four-player simultaneous play, a variety of musical genres, and a number of well-known artists. Rock Band also allows players to download new songs from the PlayStation Network and Xbox Live Marketplace. A number of instruments can be played, and players can create bands by selecting their avatar's appearance and choosing from a large variety of instruments.
 Rock Band was well received by critics, who praised the depth of the gameplay and the amount of replay value it offers, particularly in multiplayer mode. The game was also commercially successful, selling over 1.8 million copies in the United States as of January 2009.

The northern segment of the highway is maintained by ADOT , who is responsible for maintaining SR 67 like all other highways ar

ising out of the Arizona State Route System.

## Route description

The highway begins at a junction with U.S. Route 60 (US 60) in the city of Holbrook. It heads west from there to a junction with U.S. Route 180 (US 180) then turns northward through the city of Winslow, where it meets I-40 and SR 87. SR 260 turns northeast to the city of Flagstaff, passing the city of Snowflake during the route. In Flagstaff, SR 260 meets I-17, US 160, US 89, SR 89A, and SR 89. SR 260 leaves Flagstaff and heads north through the town of Williams before it meets US 160 again. It then crosses the Colorado River and enters the town of Seligman. After leaving Seligman, SR 260 turns westward towards the Grand Canyon. SR 260 meets I-40 again near the Grand Canyon, this time in the town of Tusayan. After leaving Tusayan, SR 260 turns north and ends at a junction with the Grand Canyon Scenic Highway in the town of Grand Canyon Village.

SR 260 is the only major highway that passes through the western portion of the Navajo Nation.

## History

### Navajo Bridge

Main article: Navajo Bridge

The original highway over the Colorado River was built in 1929, and connected SR 67 (the current SR 67) with US 66 (the current US 160) across the Colorado River at the eastern edge of the Grand Canyon's Marble Canyon. An additional bridge was built in 1995 to replace the old bridge.

## Future

SR 260 was planned to be reconstructed and widened from Flagstaff to US 160 in 2007; however, it is unknown if this will happen as of 2022.

## Major intersections

The entire route is in Coconino County.

Lalich states that Applewhite fit " the traditional view of a charismatic leader " , and Evan Thomas deems him a " master manip

ulator " .

In 1988, Applewhite married Helena " Sunshine " Wolff. Wolff was a former member of the Unification Church, and had been involved in a number of religious groups before meeting Applewhite. Both Applewhite and Wolff were celibate.

### Aum Shinrikyo

Applewhite became a member of Aum Shinrikyo in 1986, after a meeting with Asahara, who convinced him that the Aum Shinrikyo movement was the true religion. Applewhite initially kept his distance from Asahara, but soon became his loyal follower. He took the Aum Shinrikyo vow of celibacy and donated more than $10,000 to the movement. He was, however, not a member of the inner circle of the movement.

Applewhite and Wolff spent 1986 and 1987 in the Aum Shinrikyo compound in Altadena, California, until they moved to Osaka, Japan, in 1987. Applewhite and Wolff settled in a small apartment in the Aum Shinrikyo compound in Osaka and became a part of the Asahara group. According to Aum Shinrikyo's spokesperson, the couple moved to Japan because they wanted to work for the movement more and they were tired of California.

Asahara had a son, Masahi, with Takako Shimazu, who was a member of the movement and also served as Asahara's secretary. Masahi Asahara was born in 1970, when Takako Shimazu was a 16-year-old member of the Unification Church. In 1984, Asahara reportedly told Shimazu that he was her husband and the father of her son, and he also asked her to join Aum Shinrikyo. Shimazu married Asahara in 1987, but she was not a member of the inner circle of the group.

Later, Applewhite and Wolff became the movement's first Western couples to marry under Aum Shinrikyo's marriage ceremony. Applewhite and Wolff also acted as Asahara's spokesperson. When Asahara was arrested and charged with murder in 1995, Applewhite and Wolff were also arrested and charged with murder.

### Heaven's Gate

In 1988, Applewhite and Wolff left Aum Shinrikyo and founded Heaven's Gate. Heaven's Gate's initial goal was to convince Aum Shinrikyo to open its group to Westerners. However, when Aum Shinrikyo became the subject of increasing attention from law enforcement and the media, Applewhite and Wolff founded Heaven's Gate as a new religious movement.

Heaven's Gate was organized around the teachings of Applewhite. According to Applewhite, he had gained the ability to communicate with aliens in 1959, after an out-of-body experience. Applewhite also claimed that he had received a message from aliens telling him that "a new race was needed" and that his group would be "the new human".

Heaven's Gate's members wore black clothes, black sunglasses, and earphones. Before their deaths, the members listened to Applewhite's lectures and messages from aliens. They also followed a strict vegetarian diet, and were forbidden to have sexual relationships with humans. Applewhite denied that Heaven's Gate was a suicide cult, stating that "it's not suicide. It's just a change of clothes."

In 1992, Applewhite appeared on the Oprah Winfrey Show and discussed Heaven's Gate. In his interview, he stated that he was not a mass murderer and that he only intended to eradicate the old "human" and replace them with the new "human" in a peaceful, non-violent way.

In 1997, Applewhite and 38 other members of Heaven's Gate committed mass suicide.

The story of Snow starts when Kanata Izumo , the main protagonist , revisits a small village called Ryūjinmura ( 龍神村 , lit . "  Dragon God Village  " ) in the Tohoku region of Japan. The village is famous for the Ryūjin , a massive ancestor dragon that is the village's guardian spirit . While in the village , Kanata meets a girl named Shiina Mafuyu  ( 摘緋 真冬 , lit . "  Mafuyu Shiina  " ) who has a crush on Kanata . In turn , Kanata also develops a crush on her. Although they first meet , Kanata and Mafuyu do not get along well , yet Kanata is drawn to Mafuyu's beauty and personality .
One day , Mafuyu tells Kanata that she wants to show him something in the mountains . Together , they go to a shrine in the mountains where Mafuyu and Kanata see the Ryūjin . As they continue to look at the Ryūjin , they find an incubus that is released by Mafuyu's younger sister . The incubus that they see is the incarnation of Mafuyu's father who had died 10 years prior . The incubus begins attacking Kanata , but Mafuyu protects him . After the attack , the incubus disappears . Mafuyu then reveals that her and Kanata were in a relationship prior to the ten years . Kanata is shocked at the revelation , but Mafuyu claims that she will never love anyone but Kanata .
When Kanata wakes up the next morning , he finds himself in a strange place called the " Land of Snow " . The Land of Snow turns out to be a place between the human world and the spirit world , and the inhabitants are spirits . There , Kanata meets a girl named Shiroha  ( 白羽  , lit . " Snowy Feather  " ) who is a spirit that has 205 years of life left . Shiroha , Mafuyu and Kanata become friends and they decide to find a way to get Kanata out of the Land of Snow . In doing so , they meet the spirit of a man named Tsumugu  ( 津  , lit . "  Tsumugu  " ) who had died of illness . Tsumugu , Mafuyu and Kanata become friends , and Kanata begins to see that the Land of Snow is a better place than the human world .
In the manga, the story's premise is similar to the anime , but the characters' personalities are different . For example , Shiroha is more serious and Mafuyu is more childish . Also , Kanata is more mature and reserved .

The game was the first overtime game for both teams.

The extra point was good. Texas A&M then took the lead with 1:46 left in the quarter. Texas A&M's quarterback Jerrod Johnson completed a 16-yard pass to Ryan Swope for the touchdown. The extra point was good.
 Arkansas took their second lead of the game with 10:20 left in the second quarter. Arkansas' quarterback Ryan Mallett completed a 22-yard pass to Cobi Hamilton for the touchdown. The extra point was good. Texas A&M then took the lead with 4:29 left in the second quarter. Texas A&M's quarterback Jerrod Johnson completed a 38-yard pass to tight end Joey Hunt for the touchdown. The extra point was good. Arkansas' running back Knile Davis completed a two point conversion run.
Texas A&M took their second lead of the game with 1:18 left in the second quarter. Texas A&M's quarterback Jerrod Johnson completed a 23-yard pass to tight end Ryan Swope for the touchdown. The extra point was good.
 Arkansas took their third lead of the game with 7:02 left in the third quarter. Arkansas' quarterback Ryan Mallett completed a 75-yard pass to Jonathan Williams for the touchdown. The extra point was good. Texas A&M's running back Christine Michael completed a two point conversion run.
 Arkansas took their fourth lead of the game with 5:13 left in the game. Arkansas' quarterback Ryan Mallett completed a 21-yard pass to tight end D.J. Williams for the touchdown. The extra point was good.
 Arkansas took their fifth lead of the game with 1:05 left in regulation. Arkansas' running back Knile Davis completed a two point conversion run.
Texas A&M took their sixth lead of the game with 48 seconds left in regulation. Texas A&M's quarterback Jerrod Johnson completed a 4-yard pass to tight end Mike Evans for the touchdown. The extra point was good.
 Arkansas scored a touchdown with 6:51 left in overtime. Arkansas' running back Knile Davis completed a 4-yard run for the touchdown. The extra point was good.
 Texas A&M failed to score a touchdown with 5:53 left in overtime.
 Arkansas scored a touchdown with 1:31 left in overtime. Arkansas' quarterback Ryan Mallett completed a 2-yard pass to Dennis Johnson for the touchdown. The extra point was good.
 Texas A&M failed to score a touchdown with 1:23 left in overtime.
 Arkansas won the game.

The FLN also benefitted from the support of many of the Algerian-born French people, such as the French Communist Party member François Mitterrand , who was born in the French Algerian town of Oran .

Cole Hamels attended Meadowbrook Middle School and Rancho Bernardo High School in San Diego . He was a " gifted student " , and

was inducted into the National Honor Society in his junior year. After high school he attended the University of Texas at Arlington , where he played college baseball for the UT- Arlington Mavericks baseball team in the NCAA Division I Conference USA .
Following his college career, he was selected by the Philadelphia Phillies in the first round ( 17th overall) of the 2002 MLB Draft. He signed with the Phillies on July 16, 2002, receiving a signing bonus of $1.9 million. He made his MLB debut on September 2, 2006, against the Detroit Tigers . He was 1 for 10 with 1 walk in 9 games.
Hamels returned to the Phillies on July 23, 2006, after a brief stint with the Class A Clearwater Threshers. In his first start back, Hamels threw 8 scoreless innings against the Florida Marlins . His second start back came on August 25, 2006, in which Hamels threw a complete game, 2 hit shutout against the New York Mets at Shea Stadium.
Hamels made the 2008 All-Star team but did not pitch, as he was on the disabled list with a strained muscle in his shoulder. He was the Phillies nominee for the 2008 NL Cy Young Award and finished second to the Dodgers ' pitcher Clayton Kershaw .
He was an All-Star in 2009. He finished fourth in the Cy Young voting.
Hamels led the National League with a 2.43 ERA in 2010, and was the Phillies' nominee for the 2010 NL Cy Young Award. He finished second in the voting to San Francisco Giants pitcher Matt Cain .
Hamels was the Phillies' nominee for the 2011 NL Cy Young Award. He finished in second place, behind San Diego Padres pitcher Mat Latos .
Hamels had a 7-0 record in 13 starts in 2011 with a 2.79 ERA. He finished second in the NL Cy Young Award voting to San Francisco Giants' pitcher Matt Cain.
On June 13, 2012, Hamels pitched a shutout against the Miami Marlins , the first Phillies pitcher to throw a shutout in the National League in 2012. On July 6, 2012, Hamels tied a Major League record for most consecutive strikeouts by a pitcher in a single game with 17 straight, in Philadelphia's 2-0 win over the San Diego Padres . Hamels finished the first half of the 2012 season with a 10-3 record and a 2.69 ERA. He won the NL Player of the Month Award for June.
On October 22, 2012, Hamels was named to the 2012 MLB All-Star Game. Hamels pitched one inning against the Detroit Tigers in the 2012 World Series .
On November 7, 2012, Hamels was named one of the 30 finalists for the BBWAA 2012 NL Cy Young Award. He was ultimately chosen as the winner of the award.
Hamels was voted the Philadelphia Sports Writers Association Athlete of the Year for 2012.
On September 29, 2013, Hamels was named one of the 30 finalists for the BBWAA 2013 NL Cy Young Award.
Hamels was the Phillies pitcher against the Atlanta Braves in the 2013 NL Wild Card Game, which the Phillies lost 6-1.
On August 18, 2014, Hamels was traded to the Texas Rangers in exchange for pitching prospects Jake Thompson , Jorge Alfaro and Nick Williams .
On September 21, 2015, Hamels struck out 14 batters in a complete-game 5-0 victory over the San Francisco Giants. It was the most strikeouts for a Phillies pitcher since Jim Bunning struck out 15 on August 21, 1967.

The Cogan Spur , which is also known as the Cogan Link ( Welsh : Gyswllt Cogan ) , from the Ferry Road Interchange ( 51 @.@ 453

4 ) to the junction of the A4067 and the A4118 ( 51 @.@ 4549 ) , is part of the M4 / A4232 trunk road scheme and was constructed, with the rest of the M4 in South Wales , to improve the flow of traffic at peak times and to increase safety on the road.
 The Cogan Spur was originally built as part of the M4/A4232 trunk road scheme to relieve traffic congestion on the surrounding roads, most notably the A4067 and the A4118 , as well as to improve safety on the section of the trunk road between junctions 23 ( Cardiff ) and 24 ( Hengoed ).
 Work began on the Cogan Spur in September 1998, with the official opening taking place on 19 October 1999.
 The Cogan Spur is a single carriageway road running from a junction with the A4067 on the outskirts of Cardiff to the junction of the A4118 just north of the village of Llanrumney . The road is 1.75 miles (2.82 km) long and comprises four lanes for much of its length, with a 50 metres (160 ft) long central reservation and a cycle lane on the eastbound carriageway .
 The road is single carriageway for about the first third of its length and dual carriageway for the remainder. The first junction is with the A4067 on the outskirts of Cardiff , Leckwith . The first section of dual carriageway is 1,500 metres (0.93 mi) long and is known as the Cogan Link . The road then meets the A4118 at the Llanrumney junction .
The Llanrumney junction is a grade separated junction which is controlled by traffic lights. The northbound carriageway of the Cogan Spur passes under the A4118 and is controlled by traffic lights which are timed to allow traffic to move freely in all directions.

The magnetic field of a star is generated within regions of the interior where convective circulation occurs . This movement of

fluid occurs with respect to the stellar surface as a consequence of the release of gravitational energy, a phenomenon known as the Kelvin–Helmholtz mechanism. The release of gravitational energy occurs in the form of a star's internal luminosity.
The resulting rotation of the star creates a magnetic field and a differential in rotational speed between the equatorial and polar regions of the star. The resulting differential in rotational speed creates a differential in the force of gravity and magnetic field along the star's axis of rotation. The axis of rotation is minimally affected by the gravitational force of the star as a whole. Therefore the axis of rotation is inclined with respect to the star's interior. The magnetic field lines form as a result of the differential in rotational speed and gravity.
 The magnetic field of a star varies over time and is affected by the interaction with the stellar wind. The field is also affected by the generation of X-rays by the stellar corona. The energy released by the X-rays causes the star's magnetic field to increase in strength.

Historically , Waterfall Gully was first explored by European settlers in the early @-@ to @-@ mid @-@ 19th century , and quick

access was achieved in the late 19th century , when the Zigzag Railway was built . 

The Zigzag Railway was originally a horse-drawn narrow gauge railway that opened in 1869, and was gradually replaced by a steam powered railway in 1904.  The railway is unique in the world in that it is the only publicly operated narrow gauge railway that was built to operate steam locomotives. 

The railway is a 12-kilometre long mountain railway built to the steepest standard gauge of 4 ft 8 in (1,422 mm) , which runs from a depot at the top of Mount Dandenong to the town of Gembrook. 

The railway climbs from sea level to 408 metres above sea level.  The steepest section has a gradient of 1 in 27 ,  and the line has a total of 39 bridges and 14 tunnels. 

The railway's former 3.5-kilometre long tunnel was closed on 29 May 1931 , due to rock falls.

The railway's single track layout has been retained , with the intention of preserving the character and historical significance of the railway. 

The railway is operated by the Puffing Billy Railway, and is listed on the National Heritage Register of Australia.

## History

Mount Dandenong photograph from the 1870s

### Early history

Main article: History of the Puffing Billy Railway

The building of the railway was motivated by the need for timber as a fuel source for the Industrial Revolution.

The railway opened in 1864, to traffic in 1865 and was closed in 1952.

### Closure

The railway was closed in 1952 by the Victorian Railways, because of a decline in traffic, and a steep increase in maintenance costs.

### Preservation

Puffing Billy at Emerald Lake

In 1955, volunteers re-opened the railway on an ad hoc basis.

In 1959, the Puffing Billy Preservation Society was formed to preserve the railway.

In 1963, the present 2 ft 6 in (762 mm) narrow gauge line was opened for traffic.

In 1977, the Puffing Billy Preservation Society purchased the railway, which had been threatened with closure, from the Victorian Railways.

In 1978, the track was extended from Menzies Creek to Gembrook.

In 2012, the Puffing Billy Preservation Society purchased the former station building and land at Gembrook from the Victorian Railways.

### Connections

A 3.5-kilometre long tunnel was built between Belgrave and Menzies Creek in 1891. 

It was closed on 29 May 1931, due to rock falls.

They have a long-standing rivalry with local rivals Birmingham City , whom they play each year in the Second City Derby. The club's traditional kit colours are sky blue shirts and white shorts . The club mascot is a lion called Ronald , who has been the mascot since 1994.
 Aston Villa were formed as Villa Cross in 1874, by members of the Villa Cross Masons Lodge . They were renamed Aston Villa in 1876, and became the first ever English football league champions in 1892 . They were the first British club to win the European Cup in 1982 , beating Bayern Munich 1–0 after extra time . They also won the European Super Cup in 2000, against Lazio . Their last major trophy was the League Cup in 2010. In 2016, they reached the final of the FA Cup for the first time since 2000, but lost 2–1 to Chelsea .
Lucas is a former player at the club, having played there from 2007 to 2010. Lucas learned to play football on the streets of the Brazilian city of Goianápolis. He was discovered by a scout from his local club Clube Atlético Juventude, who invited Lucas to join the club's youth academy. He became a full-time professional footballer at Juventude in 2000, and began playing in the first team in 2001. He was described by the Brazilian media as "a new left-footed Ronaldo". Lucas's performances attracted the attention of scouts from European clubs, including Manchester United, Inter Milan and Juventus. However, he chose to join German club Schalke 04 in 2006, signing a four-year contract.
Lucas's first season at Schalke 04 was his breakthrough season. He started 38 matches in the Bundesliga, scoring three goals and providing ten assists. In his second season, Lucas played 40 games in all competitions and scored three goals. He later said of his time at Schalke 04, "I had a great time here in Gelsenkirchen. Working with the team and the coach helped me develop as a player. I am grateful for the opportunity to have played in the Bundesliga."
In the 2008–09 season, Lucas played just 21 games for Schalke 04, due to injury problems. He was also called up to the Brazil national team for the first time in January 2009. Lucas was a regular starter in his third season at the club, but suffered another injury, this time a torn cruciate ligament, in October 2009. After recovering, Lucas returned to the first team in January 2010 and helped Schalke win the DFB-Pokal, beating Stuttgart 2–1 in the final. He played 21 games in all competitions that season, scoring two goals.

However, he was regularly used as a substitute in the second half of the season, and in the 2011–12 season, he was used as a substitute for the first time in his career. Due to the lack of playing time, Lucas was strongly linked with a move away from Schalke 04. In January 2012, Lucas signed a pre-contract agreement with English club Liverpool, to join them in the summer. He made his Liverpool debut on 29 July 2012, in a pre-season friendly against Olympique Lyonnais . In the 2013–14 season, under new manager Brendan Rodgers, Lucas started to feature more regularly in the first team. He made 28 appearances in all competitions, including 26 in the league.

In his psychoanalytical study of the series , Jean @-@ Marie Apostolidès highlighted that in the Congolese adventure , Tintin r

ids himself of his fears thanks to the support of his friends and his brother. She explained this as a symptom of the phobia of losing one's own space.
I think that this interpretation is the reverse of the real cause. I can only agree with this interpretation if we consider that Tintin is in primary oral phase, as suggested in the introduction of the series. Thus, his phobias are the result of his oral phase. And only at that age, a child is afraid of losing its space: he could be separated from his mother or from the familiar environment. In this case, Tintin is not afraid of losing his space because he has become a man, but, rather, because he becomes a child. Indeed, the story The Blue Lotus is the start of the secondary oral phase, and, thus, Tintin is a child again.
The Blue Lotus is, therefore, the story of the loss of the secondary oral phase. This is the reason why Tintin is afraid of losing his space. And, at the end, he does not manage to keep it.
 The situation of the secondary oral phase is different from that of the primary oral phase. Indeed, in the primary oral phase, the child is afraid of losing its space because he is afraid of being separated from the mother. In the secondary oral phase, the child is afraid of being separated from the father, when he becomes a man. In the secondary oral phase, the child is afraid of being separated from the mother because he becomes a child again.
The Blue Lotus is the story of the loss of the secondary oral phase. Therefore, the story is the story of the loss of the adolescence.

area was cleared for the new railway line and  a gas works , the church of St Mary was built in the fort in 1883.
The fort was rebuilt in 1895 when it was raised to the status of the Government based on the new military plan.
During World War I , the fort was then equipped with a 6 inch breech-loading gun and 14000 mortar bombs.
In 1926 the first radio station experiment in the country was installed in the fort.
During World War II the fort was used as a base for anti-aircraft guns.
During the Portuguese Colonial War , the fort was used as a military hospital.
In 1992 the fort 's territory was de-militarized and turned over to the Ministry of Culture.
In 2005 a 60-day museum was opened in the fort.
The fort is now a museum open to the public.

The next year 1879 , Marsh named a more complete specimen of the same type of dinosaur , Iguanodon ( I . atherfieldensis ).

The Wilhelm Busch Prize is awarded annually to humorous and satirical poets , in memory of the great German poet, writer and illustrator Wilhelm Busch . The Wilhelm Busch Society , founded in 1930 , has been awarding the prize since 1978 .

Meyerbeer had no pupils and no direct ' school ' . Yet as his works spanned the golden age of grand opera , clear traces of his

influence can be discerned on a wide range of composers : Weber, Auber, Bellini, Wagner, Verdi, Gounod, Bizet, Massenet, Puccini, Saint-Saëns, Strauss, and Richard Strauss among them .
The possibility of hearing his works on the stage was not to be. The revolutions of 1848 and the consequent upheavals in Paris forced Meyerbeer to leave his native country and settle in Italy, where he died in 1864. His exclusion from the Paris Conservatoire, therefore, meant the loss of a potential audience and, in some cases, of a pupil.
When Meyerbeer's works were revived in Paris in 1888, a new generation of composers and singers found their way to his operas and, in the course of the last century, his works have become a regular part of the repertory.
But the most important reason for the slow recognition of Meyerbeer's genius was the composer's own character. Too much of the composer's art, like his life, is based on a sort of _Schillerian_ grandeur, a grandeur that some found too pompous, too harsh, too bombastic. This _Schillerian_ grandeur is at its best in Meyerbeer's last opera, _Le Prophète_. It is important to recall that this work was written for Paris, where grand opera is at its peak, and that it was written with a view to a particular production. In this opera Meyerbeer used the opportunity to pay tribute to French art and French artists, through arias of a sort that was not used in Italy. The subject was a French one, too: _Le Prophète_ is based on Victor Hugo's novel _Notre-Dame de Paris_ , better known to English-speaking readers as _The Hunchback of Notre-Dame_.
The ' _Schillerian_ ' nature of _Le Prophète_ was not to the taste of the Paris press. Some of the criticism is a little unfair, but no one can deny that it was very effective in discrediting the work and contributing to its long eclipse.
A related reason for the stagnation of Meyerbeer's reputation was the fact that he had no proponent in Paris, and no one who really understood his art. The composer's works were performed in the city, but not until the late nineteenth and early twentieth century did they begin to be performed with understanding. It is for this reason that the present collection, translated and edited by a composer and conductor who has devoted his life to the study of Meyerbeer's art, is so important, and why the present series of articles is so welcome.
The composer's works are now performed regularly in Paris and elsewhere. In the last twenty years, _Les Huguenots_ , _Robert le Diable_ , _L'Étoile du Nord_ , _Le Pardon de Ploërmel_ , _Les Huguenots_ and _L'Africaine_ have all been revived and _L'Étoile du Nord_ was a hit. It is important to note that they have all been staged by French theatres and under the direction of French stage directors.
It is unknown how many times Meyerbeer's works were performed during his own lifetime, but it is certain that they were very popular. There were even orchestral concerts of his overtures.
The composer's style, which is essentially a ' _Schillerian_ ' style, is so far removed from the French ideal that it is easy to understand why Parisians should have overlooked him. Tropical Storm Jose was first identified as a tropical wave that moved off the western coast of Africa on August 8 , 2005 . On

14 August 2005, the wave was upgraded to a tropical depression , and was given the name " Jose " by the National Hurricane Center (NHC). The depression strengthened into Tropical Storm Jose on August 15.
Jose was initially forecast to strengthen into a hurricane, but only reached peak winds of 50 mph (80 km/h) as it passed south of the islands of the Lesser Antilles . It then began to weaken, due to strong upper-level winds and an unfavorable environment, and on 18 August 2005, Jose was downgraded to a tropical storm. On 20 August, the storm curved westward and weakened into a tropical wave. On 22 August 2005, the tropical wave was absorbed into a frontal boundary, from which no tropical activity was expected.
Jose was the fifth tropical cyclone of the 2005 Atlantic hurricane season.
Jose formed from a westward-moving tropical wave on August 8, 2005. The wave moved across the Cape Verde Islands on August 10. The wave was recognized as a tropical depression on August 14 while centered between Hispaniola and Puerto Rico. The depression became Tropical Storm Jose and was given the name by the National Hurricane Center (NHC) at 11:00 am EDT (15:00 UTC) on August 15. The storm intensified steadily, and by 8:00 am EDT on August 16 it had strengthened into a hurricane. This was Jose's only period of strengthening, for the storm was then significantly affected by westerly shear and unfavorable outflow. The storm was downgraded to a tropical storm on August 18. The storm weakened further as it continued to the west, becoming a tropical wave on August 20. The tropical wave merged with the frontal boundary on August 22.
Jose was a compact and well-organized tropical storm. The storm had a well-defined eye, with a diameter of 7.0 mi (11.0 km). Its central pressure was 979 mbar (28.9 inHg).

The film was shot in the rocky terrain of Ramanagara , in the southern state of Karnataka , over a span of two and a half years

. The film was released in theatres on 14 June 2019 , and received mainly positive reviews . [5] The film received two nominations at the 65th Filmfare Awards South , including Best Art Director and Best Visual Effects .

## Plot

The film begins with a flashback, where the Indian Navy abandons one of its submarines in the Arabian Sea after it is damaged in a skirmish with the Pakistani Navy. After a decade, a group of people led by a policeman discover the submarine. One day, the group is attacked by a group of ghosts. The police officer contacts the Indian Navy, which sends a team of four ghost hunters to the submarine. The five arrive at the submarine, where they are briefed by the Indian Navy. They enter the submarine and start a search for the attackers. They find the bodies of the crew and the captain. They also find a recording of the attack. They play the recording and find that the ghosts were the crew of a Pakistani submarine that had attacked the Indian submarine. They also find out that the Pakistani submarine was destroyed after the attack. The four ghost hunters, who are all former Indian Navy officers, find the five spirits of the crew members and start an exorcism. They succeed and the spirits leave the submarine. However, the spirits of the captain and his first officer attack the men as a last resort; they are defeated and leave the submarine.

The film then returns to the present day, where the Indian Navy is in the process of salvaging the submarine. Later, the team of ghost hunters is reunited and informed of the salvage of the submarine. The film ends with a voiceover stating that the submarine was salvaged by the Indian Navy.

## Production

### Development

Actor Atharvaa announced his plans to produce a horror film through his home banner Anthaa Arts. The film was announced to be a ghost story based on the Ramanagara wreck, a submarine which was discovered in 2005. He was in talks with several directors to helm the project, including Venkat Prabhu, K. Rajeshwar, Karthik Naren, Venkat Prabhu, Karthik Subbaraj and Karthik Naren. He finally zeroed on Kannada director Chethan Kumar to helm the film after he met with him at a film festival.

### Casting

In October 2017, Amala Paul was confirmed to play the lead role in the film. Nassar was cast in the role of a Naval officer. In November 2017, Sneha was added to the film to play a guest role. Other cast members include Atharvaa, Prabhakar and Lal.

### Filming

The film was shot in the rocky terrain of Ramanagara , in the southern state of Karnataka , over a span of two and a half years. The makers of the film partnered with the Indian Navy and the film unit was given permission to shoot on the submarine. The film was released in theatres on 14 June 2019 , and received mainly positive reviews.

## Location

Fort Glanville is located at 1034–1050 Military Road, Glanville, near the suburb of Glenelg in the City of Holdfast Bay, in South Australia. It is located immediately to the north of the Holdfast Bay Council administration building and the Glenelg Town Hall, and approximately 250 metres north of the Glenelg Jetty and the Glenelg Foreshore. Access to the park is via the Military Road gate, which is signposted as being for access to the Holdfast Bay Council administration building.

## History

Fort Glanville was built in 1881 as one of a group of 10 forts built in South Australia to protect Port Adelaide and other ports from attack by foreign warships. It was built on a sand dune overlooking the Glenelg Bay, and the esplanade and jetty, which were then under construction. It was designed by the Engineer Corps of the South Australian Government, and built by the South Australian Public Works Department. The fort was originally named as Fort Hindmarsh after Captain John Hindmarsh the first Governor of the Colony of South Australia, but was later renamed Fort Glanville in honour of the then Premier of South Australia, Sir Thomas Glanville Gosse.

The fort was built on a gently sloping sand dune, and consisted of a series of defensive structures including a bomb-proof magazine with a 62-pound gun, a caponier, and three bunkers. It was built with a brick wall, and had a brick drainage system to deal with stormwater.

The fort was manned by the Royal Australian Artillery (RAA) from 1881 to 1903, and during the First World War. However, it was not manned during the Second World War.

In 1911, the fort was declared a Military Reserve by the South Australian Government, and was used as a training ground for the South Australian Militia, and later the Australian Army. In 1939, the South Australian Government passed a law which gave the South Australian Militia the right to use the fort.

In 1985 the South Australian Government handed the fort over to the Fort Glanville Historical Association as a community park.

The fort was listed on the now-defunct Register of the National Estate in 1983.

On September 28 , the National Hurricane Center (NHC) began tracking a tropical wave . On October 17 , the wave entered the Caribbean , and the next day the system began to show signs of organization. At 1200 UTC on October 20 , the NHC issued a Tropical Weather Outlook , indicating that a tropical depression would form within 24 hours. The NHC issued a Tropical Weather Outlook at 2100 UTC on October 20 , citing that there was a 60% chance that a tropical depression would form within 48 hours. At 1500 UTC on October 21 , the NHC upgraded the system to Tropical Depression Sixteen. The depression moved west-northwestward and strengthened into a tropical storm. From October 24 to 25 , the storm was a subtropical cyclone .

On October 22 , the hurricane center issued a Tropical Weather Outlook citing that a subtropical storm would form in 24 to 48 hours. At 1200 UTC on October 24 , the depression transitioned into a subtropical cyclone. At 0300 UTC on October 25 , the NHC initiated advisories on Subtropical Storm Sixteen. At 1800 UTC on October 25 , the cyclone transitioned back into a tropical storm. The storm made landfall in Nicaragua early on October 26 , and the next day the storm transitioned back into a subtropical cyclone. At 0400 UTC on October 29 , the NHC issued the final advisory on the storm.

## Preparations

In Nicaragua and Costa Rica , local authorities issued a Tropical Storm Watch.

## Impact

Subtropical Storm Sixteen caused flooding in Nicaragua .

Dilma Rousseff, governor of the state of Rio de Janeiro, led the bid process initially, but handed over control to the city of Rio de Janeiro after becoming president of Brazil. Palin, 44, was born in Sandpoint, Idaho, on February 11, 1964. She was the oldest of five children, and her father, Chuck Heath, a commercial fisherman, was active in the Military Order of the Purple Heart and the Veterans of Foreign Wars (VFW), so the family moved frequently. Her mother, Sally, was a homemaker and a substitute teacher. In 1982, Palin graduated from high school in Wasilla, Alaska, and then enrolled at the University of Idaho, where she studied journalism. She met her future husband, Todd Palin, a high school basketball and track star, in 1985, when they were both working as sports reporters for the local newspaper, the _Sun-Valley Daily News._

Track and field events are divided into three broad categories : track events , field events , and combined events . The major track events are sprints , middle-distance events , and long-distance events . The field events include throwing events (shot put , discus throw , and javelin throw ) and jumping events (high jump , long jump , and triple jump ). Combined events include the decathlon and heptathlon .
The term "track" may refer to the running track or the roadway for walking or running. Most often it refers to a standardized 400 m running track . This is a 200 m oval with four standardized lanes of 1.22 m (4 ft) wide, with a central 88 m straight (approx. 1/4 of a mile). The lanes are numbered 1 to 8 from the inside edge (lane 1) to the outside edge (lane 8).
Track events, as opposed to field events, take place on the flat track . They are the running events, the hurdling events, and the race walking events. The running events are sprints, middle-distance events, and long-distance events. The hurdling events are the sprint hurdle races , and the middle-distance hurdle races . The race walking events are the 20 km walk and the 50 km walk .
The sprinting events are generally 100 m , 200 m or 400 m races. In some countries, the 400 m hurdles is used as an intermediate distance event, in between the 400 m and the 110 m hurdles . The 800 m is the most common standard middle-distance event. A 1500 m race is also an intermediate distance event. The 3000 m is a long-distance event.
The most common hurdling events are 110 m hurdles and 400 m hurdles , but 100 m hurdles and 3000 m steeplechase are also standard events.
The standard race walking events are the 20 km race walk and the 50 km race walk .
In many countries, distances between 80 m and 300 m are also common in track events. These are usually run as heats or preliminary races to determine which athletes qualify for the final.

Journey 's story is told wordlessly throughout gameplay and using cutscenes . The player 's character begins on a sand dune in

1937 with the sun rising. A young boy wakes up without any clothes, and the player can interact with the boy by moving closer or farther away from him. The player can pick up a shirt, then throw the shirt to the boy, who will then put the shirt on. Unable to speak, the boy then heads to a nearby habitation, where he meets a group of children. The children tell the boy that he will have to go on a journey to find his shirt, the boy's father. The children tell the boy that his father's name is "Marcus", and that his father is a "fisherman". As the sun sets, the boy begins his journey.

## Development

### Concept

The idea for Journey came from a 2008 visit to a Japanese art museum. Thatgamecompany founder and creative director Jenova Chen remembered being inspired by a 1,500-year-old Japanese scroll painting of a mountain scene, and felt that it evoked a "sense of belonging", which he wanted to use for the next game. Chen used this idea as the basis for Journey, and created a small prototype to test his concept. Chen also wanted to "do things that we've never done before, that we don't think anyone has ever done".

Chen created an art style for Journey inspired by traditional Japanese paintings, which he liked because he thought it was a "very subtle" style. He also wanted to create a three-dimensional world that looked like it was painted. Chen stated that he wanted to create a game that was "elegant" and "subtle", and that he did not want players to feel overwhelmed by the game's narrative. He felt that there was a need for a three-dimensional, non-violent game that was about the "journey" in the same way that other games were about the "fight".

### Development history

Journey was developed by Thatgamecompany over a period of two years. The game's development began in 2009, and took two years to finish. Journey is Thatgamecompany's third game; the studio's previous games were the 2005 game Cloud and the 2008 game Flower. Chen described Journey as "our most ambitious game yet", and that it was "something that we've never done before". He said that the team was "trying to do something really different".

The development team was made up of people from Thatgamecompany, Electronic Arts, and Sony. The game was programmed using Adobe Flash, which the team felt was "easier to learn than traditional programming languages". The game was designed to "play out like a non-linear novel" with no text. The game's music was composed by Austin Wintory, who had previously worked on the soundtrack for Flower. Wintory found the experience of composing music for Journey to be "just a perfect marriage of the visuals and the sound", and felt that the music in Journey was "very different from any other game I've ever done".

### Release

Journey was first announced in 2009, and was released on March 13, 2012. The game was released on the PlayStation 3. An Xbox One port was released in 2018. The game was released digitally for PlayStation 3 via the PlayStation Network. After the game's release, Thatgamecompany released new content for the game, including three new areas to explore and a new character. The new content was released on December 11, 2012.

## Reception

Reception

Aggregate scoreReview scores

Journey received critical acclaim. Destructoid's Brett Todd gave the game a score of 10 out of 10, and called it "the best game I've played on PS3" and "an experience that I can't wait to revisit". Journey received the Game Critics Award for Best Independent Game at E3 2011. It was also nominated for GameSpot's Game of the Year 2012 award.

The game's achievement for "Agree to Disagree" is named after a line in the song "I'll Take You There" by The Staple Singers.

In the 1707 Act of Union, Maryland merged with the Province of Pennsylvania, and in 1776 the Thirteen Colonies gained independence from Great Britain.  After a period of relatively healthy growth and development, the city of Baltimore faced a period of decline and disinvestment in the late 20th century. National and international trends in technology, industry, and finance largely bypassed the city. Suburban communities enjoyed a rapid expansion, while declines in population and employment were evident in the city center. From 1950 to 1990, the city's population fell from 949,708 to 631,939. The population of the Baltimore metropolitan area, which includes not only the city but also surrounding suburban counties, declined from 2,436,827 in 1950 to 2,476,897 in 1990. Baltimore's economy and population have both been in decline, and the city has faced issues with crime and declining population since the 1960s.
However, the city has seen a rejuvenation in the 21st century. The Baltimore metro area has experienced job growth and population increases since 2000, while Baltimore city has experienced a modest population increase. The city has seen significant revitalization in many areas, including the Inner Harbor, Fells Point, and Canton, with new housing, retail, and entertainment venues. The city has also seen revitalization in its arts and cultural scene, with the construction of the Walters Art Museum addition in 2004, and the new Baltimore Convention Center in 2002, a new performing arts center in 2004, and the construction of the National Aquarium's new dolphin exhibit in 2005. The Baltimore Orioles have returned to relevance, winning the 2014 American League Wild Card. A new football stadium, which was constructed in 1998, is the site of regular Super Bowl championship games.
The city of Baltimore has one of the highest rates of population loss among major U.S. cities, and has had a decrease in population in each of the last four decades. Baltimore's population declined by 1% between 2000 and 2005, and by 2.4% between 1990 and 2000. In 2007, the Census Bureau estimated that the city had a population of 645,734. Breese was launched on 11 May 1918 out of Newport News , Virginia . She was sponsored by Gilbert McIlvaine , daughter of Breese

's commanding officer, and christened by his wife.
On 10 September 1918, the destroyer was assigned to the 1st Destroyer Squadron, U.S. Atlantic Fleet, under the command of Rear Admiral William F. Massey .
Breese was reassigned to the Atlantic Fleet's 5th Destroyer Flotilla in December 1918.
The destroyer was decommissioned on 11 June 1919 and transferred to the Reserve Fleet.
On 15 September 1920, Breese was struck from the Navy List.
Breese remained in reserve until the summer of 1940, when she was reactivated. In September she was assigned to the Atlantic Fleet, operating out of Norfolk , Virginia .
On 1 October 1940, Breese was transferred to the Pacific Fleet. She arrived at Pearl Harbor on 29 November.
Breese was reclassified DD-23 on 17 July 1940.
Breese was decommissioned on 25 January 1943 and placed in reserve.
Breese was struck from the Naval Vessel Register and sunk as a target on 24 October 1945.

In 1544 , ecclesiastical authorities in Valladolid ordered the creation of new and more sumptuous cathedral . In 1552 , an agre

emnet was reached between the diocese and the town authorities to construct a new cathedral on the site of the old one, but this was not built until 1561. The original church, a cruciform structure with a tall tower and a projecting choir, was demolished in 1562. Work on the new church was begun in 1561 . The new building was designed in the Renaissance style and its construction was supervised by the architect Juan de Herrera , who was also responsible for the construction of the Royal monastery of El Escorial . The exterior of the cathedral is simple and austere, with a single nave and three aisles.
The interior has a wide transept and a large dome with a diameter of 30 m (98 ft). The dome was designed by Juan de Herrera and built in 1585 by his son, Juan de Herrera the younger . In the place of the old crossing was placed a circular chapel , the Chapel of the Sacrament , built by the Italian architect Andrea della Porta and completed in 1573 . In the chapel are two paintings by Rubens : " The Adoration of the Magi " and " The Family of Charles I ". The choir is separated from the nave by an arch and the choir stalls date from the 18th century and were carved by local masters. In the cathedral is the tomb of the poet Quevedo, buried in 1645 . The building was damaged by fire in 1801, but was restored in 1823 .
In 1884 the cathedral was damaged by an earthquake , which destroyed many of the windows and caused the dome to collapse. The building was reconstructed in 1887 . The cathedral was damaged by the 1977 earthquake and the rebuilding was completed in the 1980s .

Jains contrast all attempts to proclaim the sole monopoly on truth with andhagajanyāyah , which can be illustrated through the

19 th century claim that the Jain Tīrthaṅkaras are incarnations of the Christian God. The Jain claim to freedom of thought is emphasized by the fact that Pūrvapakāya Jainism accepts that the Buddha was enlightened but that he did not attain nirvāṇa .
 Jainism does not accept the concept of an eternal soul or atman. The soul (jīva) is not eternal but is a succession of momentary souls (kṣipta-jīvas) that constitute a person (kṣipta-nāma).
 The causal body (karma-bhāva) is the psychological impulse of a living being that motivates its subsequent actions and is the basis of its future rebirth. The karmic body (karma-bhāva) is the total accumulation of the psychological impulses of the past, and determines the future rebirth of a living being. The karmic body of a living being is composed of the five karmic qualities (karmāṇakas, karmasattās), namely merit (puṇya), demerit (pāpa), and the three neutral qualities (arthakriya), namely knowledge (jñāna), perception (dṛiṣṭi) and conduct (cāturāgā).
 Jainism teaches that the phenomenal world is an unreal (mithyā) world. The world is composed of the five elements (pāñca tanmātras) and the twenty-four tattvas (dravya). These elements and tattvas are unreal (mithyā) because they are non-substantial (anāsthāna). However, the soul is real (satya).
 The three mendicants (tīrthaṅkars) are Mahāvīra (599–527 BCE), the twenty-fourth in the line of the Jain Tīrthaṅkaras, Parśva (872–777 BCE), the twenty-third Tīrthaṅkara, and Rishabha (840–771 BCE), the first Tīrthaṅkara.
 Siddhaṃ refers to the Sanskrit alphabet. The Jains consider the writing of Siddhaṃ sacred and prohibitively difficult to imitate. There is a strong connection between writing and knowledge. The Siddhaṃ alphabet is based on the Prakrit language, and is derived from the Brahmi script.
 Buddhists and Jains accept a common list of twenty-two Tīrthaṅkaras. Buddhists believe that the twenty-first Tīrthaṅkara was a historical person named Gautama Buddha (ca. 563–483 BCE), while Jains accept the twenty-first as Parśva.
 The three mendicants are Mahāvīra, Parśva, and Rishabha.
 The Jain concept of three bodies is derived from the Upaniṣadic concept of the body of light (prakṛti, pātāla), the body of knowledge (jñāna, jyotir) and the body of action (kriyā, mārga). Jainism extends this concept to three bodies of faith (dharma), knowledge (jñāna) and conduct (sādhanā).
 The twenty-four tattvas are a subdivision of the five elements (pāñca tanmātras) and the transitional elements (kṣetra). These are the aggregate of (saṃkhyā) elements that constitute the body (deha) or the soul (jīva). The body (deha) consists of twenty-three tattvas. The tattva of earth (bhū) is the primary material body (pṛithvī deha), the tattva of fire (agni) is the digestive fire (agnidhyās) and the tattva of water (jal) is the watery secretion (jaladhara). The tattva of air (vāyu) is the tattva of the locus of the soul (antarāyā) and the tattva of ether (ākāśa) is the soul body (jīva deha) and the soul (jīva). The tattva of life (prāṇa) is the life principle (prāṇa guṇa).

After the failure of the War of the Spanish Succession , in 1711-1712, he was again promoted to the rank of general of the army, the most important position in the Polish-Lithuanian army. In 1714 , Wiśniowiecki was appointed to the position of starost of Podolia, which he held until his death in 1744.

In 1728–1730, he was appointed the voivode of Podolia.

He died in 1744 and was buried in the Pilzno monastery in the grave of his father.

Greens Ledge Lighthouse is a sparkplug lighthouse in Connecticut , United States , off the southwest end of the Norwalk Islands

group.
It was built in 1871 by the U.S. Lighthouse Board and was first lit on 24 May of that year. It was first lit with an Argand lamp and later with a kerosene wick burner. The original light was a fixed white light. In 1898 the light was upgraded to a revolving light, with a 10-second interval. The lighthouse had a fog bell attached to it in 1897.
The lighthouse was electrified in 1924 with a 1000-watt electric bulb. The lighthouse was automated in 1973 and the light was converted to an all-red flashing light, with a 5-second interval.
The lighthouse is 13.5 m (45 ft) tall and sits on a 1.3 m (4 ft) tall foundation. It is a wood-frame tower with a brick basement. The tower is covered with vertical wood planks. The lantern is a cast iron octagonal shape. The lantern is painted white with a red roof.
The lighthouse is in the Norwalk Islands State Park. The lighthouse has been automated since 1973 and is managed by the Connecticut Department of Transportation. The lighthouse is owned by the U.S. Coast Guard.
The lighthouse remains an active aid to navigation. The lighthouse is painted white with a red roof. The lantern is painted white and there are red trim rings around the lantern.
The lighthouse is one of the most famous lighthouses in the United States and has been featured in numerous movies and television programs. In 2010, the lighthouse was used as the setting for a ransom scene in the film The Kids Are Alright . In 2012, the lighthouse was used as the setting for a scene in the television series The Good Wife .
The lighthouse is one of the most photographed lighthouses in the United States. The lighthouse has been featured in numerous magazines, calendars, and books.
The lighthouse is listed on the National Register of Historic Places .
The lighthouse is open to the public from May 1 to October 31. The lighthouse is open from 10:00 am to 3:00 pm, seven days a week. The lighthouse is closed on Thanksgiving, Christmas, and New Year’s Day.

Transmembrane proteins can also serve as ligand transport proteins that alter the permeability of the cell membrane to small mo

ieties such as ions and neurotransmitters. By facilitating the passage of these moieties across the lipid bilayer, they permit the cell to regulate its internal concentrations of, for example, sodium and calcium, which are important for cellular signaling.
Other proteins that span the cell membrane function as adhesion proteins. They bind to molecules in the extracellular matrix or to other cells. In this way, the cell is able to communicate with its environment.
Another group of proteins that span the cell membrane is the family of G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs). These proteins have seven transmembrane domains, so they are known as 7TM proteins. Each 7TM protein has an extracellular N terminus that binds to a specific ligand. The ligand then produces a conformational change that triggers a cascade of events inside the cell. In an extensively studied 7TM protein, the activity of adenosine 3',5'-cyclic phosphate (cAMP) is activated by the hormone adrenaline. The 3',5'-cyclic phosphate is a second messenger that is important in many cellular processes, including cell differentiation and cell growth.14 In other cells, the 7TM protein for the insulin-like growth factor I (IGF-I) receptor transmits a signal that stimulates the formation of cells.15 In both cases, the 7TM protein plays a key role in regulating cellular behavior.
The G-protein-coupled receptors are also involved in the regulation of cell proliferation. The receptors for IGF-I, for the growth factor epidermal growth factor (EGF), and for the hormone vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) are all 7TM proteins that regulate cell proliferation. The 7TM protein for the epidermal growth factor receptor is involved in cancer cell proliferation.16 The 7TM protein for the insulin receptor is involved in type 2 diabetes.17 The 7TM proteins involved in growth factor signaling are called tyrosine kinase receptors because the activation of the 7TM protein leads to the phosphorylation of tyrosine residues that trigger a cascade of events involved in cell growth and cell differentiation. In the case of the insulin receptor, the primary effect is to stimulate the entry of glucose into the cells.
The transmembrane proteins that bind to growth factors are often glycosylated. The glycosylation sites are usually located on the extracellular domain. Glycosylation may be either O-linked or N-linked. N-linked glycosylation is more common in 7TM proteins. It is catalyzed by glycosyltransferases that are called N-acetylglucosamine transferases. The N-glycans are then either further processed by the glycosyltransferases or they are removed by the action of the proteo-glycanase Fru4.18
In 7TM proteins, the entire extracellular domain is involved in ligand binding.19 When a 7TM protein binds to its ligand, the ligand is normally located in the same plane as the extracellular domain. This is the case for the insulin receptor and the glucagon receptor.20 The ligand binding is not restricted to 7TM proteins. In fact, some proteins that do not span the membrane can bind to ligands. For example, the integrin family of 7TM proteins bind to extracellular ligands such as laminin.
Although 7TM proteins are involved in regulating cellular behavior, they may also be involved in the regulation of protein activity. The enzyme phosphodiesterase, for example, has a 7TM protein, PDE4A1, that is responsible for the targeting of the enzyme to the plasma membrane.21 The PDE4A1 protein is able to bind to the nucleotide cAMP, thereby regulating the enzyme activity. This illustrates how the regulation of the membrane protein activity can involve the regulation of membrane protein localization.

Super Mario Land is a side-scrolling platformer , similar to the original Super Mario Bros. The gameplay is simple , with Mario running and jumping . He can also shoot fireballs as a weapon, with a power-up that makes him invincible for a short time .
The game's levels are divided into fourteen sections with three stages each . Each stage has a midway point, and the player can return to a previous stage if need be. The player has three lives as in the original Super Mario Bros . , but if Mario is hit by an enemy or falls into a trap, he loses a life. The game has a password system to continue playing after a game is lost . The game also includes a timer, which can be disabled . The timer counts up to 9:59, and once it reaches 10:00, the game is over . The player can keep track of the time in the pause menu .
The first stage is a desert with palm trees and rocks . There are no enemies and no power-ups . The second stage is a forest with a bridge to cross . Enemies include Goombas , Koopas , and Piranha Plants . The third stage is a cave with water , and contains Warp Whistles . The fourth stage is a beach with a lighthouse . The fifth stage has a seabed with a submarine . The sixth stage is a swamp with a castle and a poisonous swamp . The seventh stage is a volcano with a lava pit and a boss battle with Tatanga . The eighth stage is a desert . The ninth stage is a forest . The tenth stage is a tropical island with a submarine . The eleventh stage is a dark forest . The twelfth stage is a castle with a boss battle with Tatanga . The thirteenth stage is a submarine with a submarine battle with Tatanga . The final stage is a town with a boss battle with Tatanga .

While crossing Madagascar on a westward trajectory , Domonia weakened ; JTWC estimated the winds decreased to 55 km / h ( 35 mp

/ h ) on October 26. The next day, the cyclone intensified again and reached maximum intensity, with winds of 155 km / h ( 95 mp / h ) and a minimum pressure of 968 mbar . The cyclone then passed through the area of Madagascar's Reunion Island and Mauritius , where it caused heavy rains and winds. On November 1, Domonia was downgraded to a tropical storm and continued moving towards the west. On November 3, the storm was downgraded again to a tropical depression.
On August 28, the tropical storm Domonia developed from the remnants of the tropical depression Linda . The cyclone was named by the Mauritius Meteorological Service, which is the first time that the agency has given a name to a tropical cyclone.

At the start of the 1962/3 season , Roy was sold to Everton for £100,000 – the biggest fee ever paid by a First Division club at the time, and one that both Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur were so upset by that they threatened to withdraw from the First Division .
 Rovers manager Bill Shankly later admitted that he had little choice but to sell: "I was forced to sell him. He had no future at Everton. All he did was score goals and I needed to strengthen other areas of the team.
Mike Trebilcock was one of the players who was signed to fill the void left by the sale of Greaves, and a record-breaking £100,000 was duly spent on him.
 The move was a great success, with Trebilcock playing a vital role in Everton's eventual title-winning side that season, and he later admitted that the move to Merseyside was a turning point in his career: "If I hadn't moved to Everton I'd have ended up like Greavsie. I'd have been living in a flat and having a drink every day. I may have been the best player in the Second Division, but I'd have been a bum."
 "I think it's fair to say that (Trebilcock's) signing was a turning point in Everton's history. We went out and bought him and he scored the goals which got us into the title race. Without Trebilcock, Everton would probably have been fighting in mid-table that season."
Roy said: "It was a big blow to me to leave Arsenal, because I always felt I was the best player in the First Division. I'd never seen myself as a Second Division player, but my big mistake was letting Shankly talk me into it. I had no intention of leaving Arsenal, but I couldn't turn down Everton's offer. I'd never seen so much money in my life."
Trebilcock scored 27 goals in his first season at Everton , including one against his former club, Arsenal, at Highbury. He was a member of the Everton side that won the First Division title in 1963 , and he scored 11 goals in 1963/4 as Everton finished third in the league.
 "In the first half I was awful. I didn't even get near the ball. But I was so desperate to make up for it, I kept going until I scored. It was one of the happiest days of my life."
Trebilcock went on to make 117 appearances for Everton and scored 37 goals, before moving on to Lincoln City in 1966 , where he spent the next two seasons. He was then signed by St Mirren, where he stayed for four years, and then he ended his playing career at Ross County.

Halo 3 is a first-person shooter, in which the player, as the Master Chief, uses a variety of weapons and vehicles to fight the Covenant.
The titles in the Halo franchise are notable for the ability to move while aiming, a feature referred to as "free aiming".[1] In addition, the games include a regenerating health system and the ability to sprint, both of which were popularized in first-person shooters by the original Halo.
Halo 3 has 15 multiplayer maps, with several of them being based on locations from Halo 2.
The multiplayer mode also features a new gametype known as Firefight, in which the player is placed with four other players and must stay alive against waves of increasingly strong enemies.
The game has been praised by critics and has sold well, but has also attracted criticism for its steep learning curve.
Halo 3 is the first game in the Halo franchise to have full support for the Xbox 360 vision camera, which allows players to use the Xbox 360's camera to take pictures of their gameplay.
Also new to the series is a co-operative campaign mode.

On 29 April, however, the UN Air Force destroyed 80 percent of North Korea's air force, and the air attacks ceased. The destruction of the North Korean air force was a great victory for the UN Air Force, which had been built up over the past decade.

The 2nd Battalion was accompanied by a reconnaissance platoon from the 27th Engineer Battalion, which was equipped with flame throwers and explosives. They were to destroy the bridge and then fall back to Taegu.

On 3 May, the 1st Marine Brigade, which had landed at Pohang, was ordered to move north to reopen the road between Taegu and Pohang.
Over the next several days, the 1st Marine Brigade and the 21st Regimental Combat Team were pushed back to Taegu, and the North Korean 6th Division was able to secure a position south of the city.

State Route 67 ( SR 67 ) is a 43 @.@ 4 mi ( 69 @.@ 8 km ) long , north – south state highway in northern Arizona . Also called

9th Avenue in Flagstaff , the highway serves the city as a commuter road and through route . It was previously part of U.S. Route 66 ( US 66 ) .
SR 67 begins southeast of Flagstaff in the city of Bellemont , where it is called 9th Avenue . It leaves the city and heads northwest through mostly rural areas until it reaches SR 180 , which it meets at a trumpet interchange . SR 67 then continues northwest through the unincorporated community of Sunnyside .
SR 67 serves as an alternative to Interstate 40 ( I-40 ) and US 180 . It is not a major transportation artery, with a 2011 average daily traffic count of 1,700 vehicles north of Flagstaff and 680 vehicles south of the city.
1937 Arizona State Route 67 was established between US Route 80 ( US 80 ) in Williams and US 89 in Flagstaff . The highway was named US Route 66 in 1938. US 66 was realigned to bypass Flagstaff to the southeast in 1950. The realignment was designated State Route 66 in 1951.
When US 66 was decommissioned in 1985, SR 67 was legislated in 1986 to run from the former end of US 66 at I-40 east to SR 180 ( US 180 ) in Flagstaff. The new southern terminus of the route was located in the Flagstaff city limits, where it was known as 9th Avenue.
The northern terminus was in Winslow , where it overlapped SR 87 at an intersection . SR 67 was extended to the United States – Mexico border in 1988, connecting it to SR 80 in Yuma . In 1989, SR 67 was extended north from US 87 in Winslow to SR 89 in Flagstaff, eliminating the overlap.
In 1997, SR 67 was extended north from Flagstaff to SR 180 at the intersection of what is now known as the interchange at SR 67.
As part of a larger reconstruction of the intersection of SR 67 and I-40 in Flagstaff, the interchange was reconstructed in 2007. The intersection was rebuilt in 2013, including the construction of a roundabout.

A transit of Venus across the Sun takes place when the planet Venus passes directly between the Sun and a superior planet , bec

aming visible as a small black disc silhouetted against the solar disk. Venus and Earth have nearly the same size, their diameters are 0.722 and 0.724, and the distance between them is about 100 million km. At such a distance Venus is in the same plane as Earth's orbit, so it is a very rare event.
The first transit of Venus was observed in 1631 by Jeremiah Horrocks , he was the first to predict it using his own calculations. The first transit of Venus predicted by Newton was in 1665, but he died before he could witness it. In 1761 the first set of transits of Venus was observed by astronomers on both sides of the Atlantic. Although they were not in contact, they had the same results and the calculations were the same. The next transit of Venus occurred in 1874 and the last one in 2004.
The transit of Venus will be observed on June 5, 2012. It will be the last of a series of four transits that began in 2004 and will continue in 2012, 2016 and 2020.

abana Azmi ) , are shown to be both followers of the Sufi saint Shah Abdul Latif Bhitai , despite being Hindu and Muslim.
The film is set in the fictional village of Uttar Sham ( an allusion to Pakistan ) in 1947 , where Saket is a teacher in a mission school and Amjad is a lawyer.
Saket is ready to leave the village and take up a teaching job in Lahore , while Amjad and her husband want to move to Pakistan.
The village's Christian priest , Father Joseph ( played by Pankaj Kapur ) , tells the villagers that the two friends have been having nightly visits from "someone" who tells them to "follow the path of peace, love and forgiveness" .
One night , Saket sees the saint ( played by Naseeruddin Shah ) , who tells him that he has been sent to wake him from his slumber and tell him to prepare for a great journey. The saint calls Saket "Mohamed Rafi" and Saket is shown to be a Sufi .
Amjad's husband , the doctor ( played by Prakash Raj ) , discovers that the "visitor" is in fact Shah Abdul Latif Bhitai , who has been brought to the village as a patient.
He cuts off the saint's hands and feet to prevent him from "walking" , and the saint dies.
In the last scene , the doctor sees the saint's face in the moon, and the two friends are shown to be sitting under a tree in Lahore , listening to the singing of the Sufi saint.
Shah Abdul Latif Bhitai ( c1689-1752 ) was a Sufi saint from Sind, in what is now Pakistan.
He was the author of the renowned Book of Love ( Seedhee-No-Shah ) , in which he wrote poems in the style of the classical poet Amir Khusrau .

Chasing Vermeer is a 2004 children 's art mystery novel written by Blue Balliett and illustrated by Brett Helquist . Set in Hyd

ra, Greece, the story centers on two preadolescent students, Calder and Petra. The novel was an instant New York Times bestseller and was nominated for a National Book Award for Young People 's Literature in 2004. According to a 2009 interview with the author, Balliett initially wrote Chasing Vermeer as a short story.
Chasing Vermeer is the first book in the "Chasing Vermeer" series.
Calder Pillay and Petra Andalee are two students at the Hydra School of Art in Greece. Calder is a 12-year-old boy with an interest in birds and insects, while Petra is an 11-year-old girl with an interest in ancient art. Their teachers are a 56-year-old man named Mr. Vernon, who teaches art history and plans to retire soon, and a 29-year-old woman named Ms. Flynn, who teaches art appreciation. Their classmate, Tommy, is a 10-year-old boy with a severe stutter.
On their first day of class, they are introduced to their new classmates: a 13-year-old boy named Julian, who is interested in science, and a 12-year-old girl named Sonia. A few days later, Mr. Vernon and Ms. Flynn arrive late to class after a fight over art appreciation. Julian and Sonia disappear, and the class believes they have been kidnapped.
The book ends with Calder, Petra, and a few of their classmates following a trail of bread crumbs to a cave, where they find a secret door to a room filled with paintings. The paintings are a copy of Johannes Vermeer 's painting "The Music Lesson" and appear to have been created by two children.
The following books in the series are The Wright 3 and The Calder Game.
Chasing Vermeer won the 2004 Edgar Award for Best Juvenile Mystery.
